chapters.title: Council staff opens hearing and gives procedural instructions

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning, good morning.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Welcome to the New York City Council Committee on Finance, joint with Housing and Building.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, we ask that you please silence all electronics.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: If you wish to fill out an appearance card, please see one of the sergeant at arms in the back.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff

chapters.summary: Councilmember Pierina Ana Sanchez, Chair of Housing and Buildings, welcomes attendees to the joint oversight hearing on Advancing Homeownership Opportunity and Protection. She acknowledges her personal care matter, lists present council members, and thanks the speaker for flexibility.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez opens joint hearing on homeownership, acknowledges colleagues

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Pierina Sanchez, Chair of the Committee on Housing and Buildings.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Welcome to today's joint oversight hearing with Chair Linda Lee and the Finance Committee on Advancing Homeownership Opportunity and Protection.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you also to the speaker for her flexibility.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm dealing with a personal care matter, but I will be here for a few hours today because this matter is so important.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I want to acknowledge my colleagues who are present today, Councilmember...

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Salam, sorry, I'm very short.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Councilmember Salam Narcisse.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Deputy Speaker Williams, Councilmember Wong, Councilmember Carl Wilson, and Councilmember Justin Sanchez.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Oh, and Councilmember Marte, and Councilmember, so many names, last name Morano.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Yes, Morano.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And Councilmember Jim Gennaro on Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Sanchez discusses the dream of homeownership and the rising costs, taxes, and insurance that threaten it. She cites statistics: 66% of first-time foreclosure auctions are single/two-family homes, deed theft complaints tripled from 2023 to 2025, and over 10,000 homes were flipped between 2021 and 2025, disproportionately in Black and brown neighborhoods.
chapters.title: Sanchez outlines homeownership crisis, foreclosure and deed theft data

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: For generations, working families across the city have sacrificed, saved, and worked themselves to the bone for the chance to own a little piece of New York.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Not just for a roof over their heads, but for the stability that it brings, the roots it allows them to put down, and the possibility of passing something on to their children.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: That is the dream of homeownership.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And in a city built by working people, we should be doing everything in our power to protect it.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Instead, we're watching that dream become harder and harder to achieve and harder to keep.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: For families who sacrifice to buy a home, taxes, insurance, utilities, and repair costs keep rising as buildings age.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: For older Black and Latino homeowners especially, financial distress can put their generational wealth at risk.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: In the third quarter of 2026, single and two-family homes together represented 66% of New York City's first-time foreclosure auction cases.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And to make matters worse, predatory activity is on the rise.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Between 2023 and 2025, complaints of deed theft more than tripled.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Between 2000 and 2020, New York City lost

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: more than 185 non-Hispanic black residents.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Rising housing costs are part of that story, but research from the Pratt Center shows us and found that more than 10,000 New York City homes were flipped between 2021 and 2025, disproportionately in black and brown neighborhoods.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: We have to ask, is the city doing all that we can to prevent speculation from pricing working families out of the very neighborhoods that they helped to build?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And is our city equipped to track how many homes are moving from owner occupants into investor hands?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: These specific pressures affect Michilama and HDFC co-ops, market co-ops and condos, single-family homeowners, and small owner-occupied multifamily buildings differently.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Co-op boards face costly repairs and governance challenges.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Small property owners juggle expenses and responsibilities with their tenants.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And for New Yorkers trying to buy their first home, the median first-time buyer recently put down $265,000 on an $883,000 home.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: That's only about one-third of the city's households who are owning their homes, and in the Bronx, in my neck of the woods, barely one in five.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: What kind of opportunity is this for a working family?

chapters.summary: Sanchez recalls past hearings and council efforts, including a 4% homeownership target and HPD term sheet updates. She introduces bills in the package, such as Intro 861 and 862 by Councilmember Brooks-Powers, and others by Councilmembers Riley, Narcisse, Hudson, Williams, Hankerson, and Deputy Speaker Williams, thanking her team and staff.
chapters.title: Sanchez reviews past council work and introduces bills in package

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: We've been working on these issues for years in the council, from our comprehensive hearing in 2023 on home ownership to hearings on Michilamas this summer, co-op transparency, deed theft, distressed properties, and the mayor's overall housing plan.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: We've pressed HPD to update.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: its home ownership term sheets and enacted a 4% home ownership opportunity target in the last administration.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Today, we want to hear this administration's plan.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Are she and D tax payment plans and D theft protections reaching families before they lose their homes?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Are home first, the homeowner help desk, which shout out to Councilmember Brooks Powers, her bill created, and the Office of the Homeowner Advocate Voucher Homeownership, tax incentives like J51 and HPD's development programs, are these things meeting the need?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: We look forward to exchanging ideas with the administration and collaborating to keep homeownership a real possibility for more New Yorkers, including discussion of my colleagues'bills before us today.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Intro 861, sponsored by Councilmember Brooks Powers, for example, would expand outreach about the Housing Choice Voucher Homeownership Program, which helps voucher holders transition into ownership.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Intro 862, also sponsored by Councilmember Brooks Powers, would expand the Home First down payment assistance program so that at least 600 New Yorkers a year would receive the financial assistance they need to make down payments.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: In addition to these bills, which would give direct financial assistance to potential home buyers, Councilmember Riley's Intro 406, Councilmember Narciso's 1091, Councilmember Hudson's 1084, and Deputy Speaker Williams'Intro

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: 109 would create protections for current homeowners.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: While Councilmember Hankerson's Intro 1082 and Deputy Speaker Williams'Intro 1097

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: would help us understand why New Yorkers are struggling to purchase homes so that we together with the administration can better serve the public.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I want to take a moment to thank Deputy Speaker Natasha Williams for leading this package and the Black, Latino, and Asian Caucus for championing Black homeownership.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I thank my team, Ben Ratner, Kim Castellanos, Gerard Fernandez, Malia Sardinia,

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Marcus Khan, Geraldine Feliz, Emily Portalin-Mendez, Maria Jose Mares, I got a big team, y'all, Soraya and Oriana, and the committee staff here today, Austin Malone, Billy Eck, Jose Conde, Dirk Spencer, Mohamed Shadid, and Noah Slossberg,

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Carla Naranjo, and Spencer Kroon.

chapters.summary: Sanchez concludes her remarks and turns the floor over to co-chair Councilmember Linda Lee to deliver her remarks.
chapters.title: Sanchez turns over to co-chair Linda Lee

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I will now turn it over to co-chair, Councilmember Linda Lee, to deliver her remarks.

chapters.summary: Councilmember Linda Lee, Chair of Finance, thanks colleagues and co-chairs, and introduces the oversight hearing. She discusses Intro 1084, which would require automatic enrollment in property tax payment plans, and shares her experience as a nonprofit leader and council member.
chapters.title: Chair Lee welcomes attendees, outlines Finance Committee bills

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Before I begin, we've been joined by Council Members Riley, Aviles, Brooks-Powers, and Abreu.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I know it's a little toasty, so hopefully you all won't fall asleep during the hearing.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: It's exciting stuff.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I'm Council Member Linda Lee, Chair of the Committee on Finance, and would like to thank my colleagues and co-chairs, Council Member Perriana Sanchez, Chair of the Committee on Housing and Buildings, and Deputy Speaker Nantosha Williams for joining me this morning for this

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: important oversight hearing on advancing homeownership opportunity and protection.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Today we will hear a package of legislation intended to promote homeownership opportunities and fortify protections for current and prospective homeowners in New York City, including Intro 10.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: which falls under the jurisdiction of the Committee on Finance.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Intro 1084, co-sponsored by Councilmember Crystal Hudson, would require the Commissioner of Finance to automatically enroll individuals in a Department of Finance-administered residential property tax payment plan that requires an individual to pay the lowest total amount.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: The commissioner would be required to notify an eligible individual about automatic enrollment at least 60 days before the first payment is due under the applicable plan, the types of plans for which the individual is eligible and their costs,

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: the plan in which the individual is enrolled, and any steps necessary to complete enrollment.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Additionally, the commissioner would be required to establish a plainly and conspicuously communicated opt-out mechanism that would allow an individual to decline automatic enrollment at the time the individual receives the notice.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Throughout my time serving as a nonprofit leader and now as a council member, I've seen how crucial homeownership resources are to my constituents as they navigate the many facets of owning a home in this great city,

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: including navigating various city offices and agencies when faced with questions or hardships related to homeownership.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Owning a home can be very difficult, and it is our responsibility as lawmakers to make it easier for homeowners to seek help and support when they feel overwhelmed or burdened, rather than adding to the challenges of navigating the complexities of city government.

chapters.summary: Lee expresses excitement to hear from DOF, HPD, and DOB representatives, and thanks Finance Committee staff. She then passes the floor back to Chair Sanchez.
chapters.title: Lee thanks agencies and staff, passes back to Chair Sanchez

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I'm excited that we are able to convene representatives from DOF, HPD, and DOB to better understand how we can continue to make homeownership a reality.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: for more New Yorkers, while also ensuring that current homeowners have the resources and support they need to afford and remain in their homes.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you to my colleagues for joining me today, to DOF and the other agencies for testifying, and to the Finance Committee staff, Emra Adev, Daniel Krupp, Jack Story, Delara

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Dimnaku, Andrew Wilbert, Lyle Reed, Carla Narando, Owen Katowski, Brian Sarfo, and Spencer Kuhn.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I think we recognized everybody, right?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, and I'll pass it back to Chair Sanchez.

chapters.summary: Sanchez thanks Chair Lee and calls on Councilmember Brooks-Powers to speak, followed by Deputy Speaker Williams.
chapters.title: Sanchez calls on Councilmember Brooks-Powers

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Lee.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So I'll now turn it over to Councilmember Brooks Powers, followed by Deputy Speaker Williams.

chapters.summary: Brooks-Powers discusses her district's high homeownership rates and introduces Intro 861 to expand outreach about the Housing Choice Voucher Homeownership Program, and Intro 862 to strengthen the Home First down payment assistance program to help at least 600 first-time homebuyers annually.
chapters.title: Brooks-Powers presents Intro 861 and 862 for homeownership outreach and down payment aid

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Lee, Chair Sanchez, and members of the Committees on Finance and Housing and Buildings for including Intro 861 and Intro 862 in this critical hearing on homeownership.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: I have the privilege of serving communities where homeownership has long been a cornerstone of neighborhood stability and economic opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: In my district, roughly half of all households own their homes, and nearly 7 in 10 of those homeowners are black.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: For generations, families in Southeast Queens have worked hard, saved, and sacrificed to buy homes and build something lasting to pass down to their children and grandchildren.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: But rising costs and limited access to available resources are putting that goal out of reach for too many New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Citywide, fewer than one in three households own their home, including just 26% of black households and 17% of Latino households.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: We cannot talk about building a more affordable New York without addressing both sides of this challenge.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Helping existing homeowners stay in their homes and creating meaningful opportunities for the next generation to become homeowners.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: My bills together prioritize outreach and access for resources to the city.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: The city already funds.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: to make sure that potential homeowners are aware and eligible for the tools we have in place.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Intro 861 would require HPD to launch an education and outreach campaign so Section 8 voucher holders know about the Housing Choice Voucher Home Ownership Program.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Which lets eligible families put their voucher towards buying a home.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: The campaign would explain who is eligible and how to apply in every designated citywide language.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Access to opportunity begins with knowing it exists.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Intro 862 would strengthen the city's Home First program by requiring HPD to help at least 600

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: first-time homebuyers every year with down payment and closing costs, and to report annually on how many families were helped and the communities where they bought.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: As of January 2025, HPD reported Home First had helped over 1,100 New Yorkers in the past decade, a little over 100 a year.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: The council has since secured funding to double the city's investment in the program, and Intro 862 makes sure that investment reaches families at scale.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Together, these bills expand pathways to first-time homeownership and help more working families build equity, establish roots, and create generational wealth so New Yorkers can afford to stay in the city they call home.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Thank you to the advocates who continue to fight.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: for affordable homeownership across New York City, including the Center for New York Homeownership, where I am proud to serve on the board, and many others.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Thank you as well to my colleagues for their work on this package.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: I look forward to working with the chairs and the committees to move Intro 861 and Intro 862 forward.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Sanchez thanks Brooks-Powers and calls on Deputy Speaker Nantasha Williams to speak.
chapters.title: Sanchez calls on Deputy Speaker Williams

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Council Member.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'd now like to call on Deputy Speaker Williams.

chapters.summary: Williams highlights the new Homeownership Opportunity Protection Package and community engagement efforts, including homeownership expos. She introduces Intro 1096 to identify and assist communities at risk of displacement, and Intro 1097 to study disparities in DOB enforcement.
chapters.title: Deputy Speaker Williams discusses homeownership package and Intro 1096, 1097

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chairs.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: And I really appreciate your leadership, your flexibility, your support in hosting this hearing today.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: And before I get into my bills, I just want to say that the council's commitment to homeownership doesn't just extend legislatively, and we're excited to hold this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: But this year, we also created a new initiative under the leadership of Finance Chair Lee called the Homeownership Opportunity Protection Package.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: And we actually increased the amount of money that goes to organizations supporting all facets of homeownership, whether you want to buy a home, whether you need support for foreclosure or deed theft, as a few examples.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: And then in addition to what we've been doing financially through our initiatives is also a community engagement piece.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: We have a community engagement unit in the council, and we are going to every single borough to host a home ownership expo.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: We believe we need to meet people where they are.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: and leverage our resources to do that.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: We held our first one in Queens, and we look forward to going to Brooklyn in January.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: So this is a full comprehensive effort that the council has undertaken under the leadership of Speaker Menon to really help our homeowners.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: We love tenants.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: We love tenants.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: And I think this city and this state does a lot for tenants, but they do not do enough for homeowners.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: And homeowners struggle too.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: And so, again, excited to be here in Southeast Queens.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I represent a community that is majority homeownership, which is not like the rest of the city.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: A home can represent decades of work and something a family hopes to pass on to the next generation.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: For a homeowner facing a foreclosure notice, a suspected deed theft, or a costly building violation, getting the right help early can make a real difference.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: My first bill, Intro 1096, would require the city to identify the community districts at greatest risk of displacement each year and use that information to guide outreach.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Homeowners should be able to get clear information about tax relief, free legal help, and how to spot predatory offers.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I want to know how the city will reach people who may never find that information online and what happens after someone asks for help.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: My second bill, Intro 1097, would require DOB to study whether enforcement and compliant outcomes vary by race, geography, or income.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I want to understand what happens after a violation.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: is issued?

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: How long does it take to get a correction plan approved or a re-inspection completed?

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Are homeowners with similar violations seeing different outcomes depending on where they live, where the study finds disparities?

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: We hope it would recommend changes.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I look forward to hearing what the agencies are doing today to support homeowners and listening also to their comments on all of the bills in today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Wanting to really understand where homeowners are still getting stuck and what the city can do to commit to doing more for homeowners in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: So thank you so much again to all my colleagues who have bills in this package.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I'm really excited to be here and I look forward to the discussion.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Deputy Speaker.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And thank you for your leadership on this.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: It's a really impressive package that you put together with all of our colleagues.

chapters.summary: Sanchez thanks Williams and calls on Councilmember Mercedes Narcisse, followed by Councilmember Morano.
chapters.title: Sanchez calls on Councilmember Narcisse

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I now want to call on Councilmember Narcisse, followed by Morano.

chapters.summary: Narcisse discusses the struggle of Black and brown homeowners and introduces Intro 1091 to protect homeowners from unexpected property tax liens by requiring clear, timely notifications and transparent explanations. She explains the bill's requirements for DOB and DOF.
chapters.title: Narcisse presents Intro 1091 on property tax lien notifications

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Good morning and thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Thank you, Deputy Speaker.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I recall when you called me about the package, I was so excited.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I am here to look for ways to help homeowners to keep their home.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And it's such a struggle.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: For black and brown communities, as you know, going to so much, and they work triple jobs, the CNA, the HHA, the nurses that struggle to get a home

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: and to lose it, there goes their all hard work and for the next generation of their family.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So 1091, it's a very important step toward protecting New York City homeowners.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And I want to step back a little further because when we say black and brown, there's a lot of low-income folks.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And when we say low-income folks, unfortunately, I'm always looking at the statistic and the data.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: They pinpoint me toward the black and brown.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: But all the lower-income areas that's suffering with a home in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: What I want to do is to protecting New York City homeowners from unexpected property tax liens by requiring a clear...

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Timely notifications and very transparent with the explanation.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Because we all know when you stress and you don't have no money, any paper that come in your

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: bill, I mean your mailbox to pay bills, it gives you more frustration.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So we have to be very clear and transparent with the direction of the violation.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: To give information for people to avoid, remove, or remove the liens on their home.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: This bill will promote accountability and gives homeowners a fair opportunity to resolve the outstanding debt.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Before losing the equity in their homes.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Homeowners deserve that.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: They deserve the transparency.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And we all can agree with that.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So this bill is actually, force the hand, I don't know what to say, Department of Building.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Notices of violation that can be enforced as a tax lien would have to warn that on an unpaid ECB judgment may lead to a lien on the property in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Within three days of an ECB judgment,

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: DOB, Department of Building, must notify the owner by mail or email.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: The notice must include a plan language.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: We know that when language is complex, people are not getting it fully.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So the breakdown of the charge.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Payment deadlines and option and the steps to avoid or remove a lien and return to compliance.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: DOB and DOF would publish annual data

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: on lien conversions by community district and conduct outreach to one and two family homeowners facing the sling that they're doing because that would be very helpful.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: It will take effect in 120 days after becoming a law.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And I think you all can agree with that.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: We don't want people to lose their home.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So I rest to that.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Chair.

chapters.summary: Sanchez thanks Narcisse and calls on Majority Leader Shaun Abreu to speak.
chapters.title: Sanchez calls on Majority Leader Abreu

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'd now like to call on Majority Leader Abreu.

chapters.summary: Abreu raises concerns about the expiring DAMP tax exemption in 2029, which creates uncertainty for HDFCs seeking financing. He introduces Resolution 9 calling on the state to extend the exemption in perpetuity and provide additional relief.
chapters.title: Abreu advocates for Resolution 9 to extend DAMP tax exemption for HDFCs

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, chairs, and thank you to the administration for coming to testify.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: My district has the highest concentration of HDFCs in New York City, and I want to raise an issue that is causing significant concern for several homeowners in my district, many of which are in this room, and many of which are in the overflowing room as well.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: As you know, the DAMTAC exemption is set to expire in 2029, and there is still no certainty about its extension.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: This uncertainty has real consequences for HDFCs, many of which are struggling to secure loans and financing from banks that are reluctant to lend without knowing what their future property tax obligations will look like.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: And that's why I've introduced Resolution 9, which calls on the state to pass legislation extending the damp tax exemption in perpetuity and providing additional financial relief to HDFCs.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I was happy to see the rental to co-op conversions included in the mayor's housing plan.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: particularly through the new Our Home program.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: But the one thing is for sure is that cities'investment in affordable homeownership cannot end at initial conversion.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: These buildings age, they face significant capital needs, and the shareholders and board members are often first-time homeowners who are suddenly responsible for navigating very complex financial, regulatory, and building management systems.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: So I look forward to hearing later on your testimony on HCFCs and the much-needed extension, damp tap exemption, that my constituents and many constituents of our city very much need.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

chapters.summary: Sanchez thanks Abreu and calls on Councilmember Frank Morano to speak.
chapters.title: Sanchez calls on Councilmember Morano

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And now, Councilmember Morano.

chapters.summary: Morano argues for making it easier for New Yorkers to access benefits they're entitled to. He introduces Resolution 599 calling on Albany to establish a centralized income verification system for income-based homeowner property tax exemptions, similar to the Enhanced STAR program.
chapters.title: Morano presents Resolution 599 for centralized income verification for tax exemptions

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair, and thank you for remembering my name with such ease this time.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm going to call you Morano from now on, and I'll never forget it again.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I'll take it.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I may have to just speak out more so I leave more of an impression.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I want to thank you for holding this important hearing and for including my resolution 599.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: You know, we spent a lot of time in this council talking about creating new benefits for New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I would argue that we ought to spend just as much time making sure New Yorkers can actually access the benefits we've already promised them.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So, I mean, imagine being a 78-year-old widow living on a fixed income in a home you and your husband spent 40 years paying off.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: You're struggling with rising insurance premiums, rising utility bills, rising cost of groceries, nothing.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: seems to ever go the other way.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Then, because you missed a renewal notice or misplaced a financial document, you lose a property tax exemption that you're legally entitled to receive.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: That is crazy, and it's a failure of government.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: My resolution calls on Albany to establish a centralized income verification system for income-based homeowner property tax exemptions, including those for seniors

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: and people with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: The good news is that we don't have to reinvent the wheel.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: New York State already uses a similar mechanism for the Enhanced STAR program, and there's something

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: fundamentally absurd about one arm of government asking a senior citizen to repeatedly produce financial information that another arm of government already possesses.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So this proposal would help reduce administrative costs, it would improve accuracy, it would prevent fraud, and it would make life a little easier for homeowners.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It doesn't seek to change who qualifies for these benefits at all.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It doesn't create any new entitlements.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It seeks to make the process of determining eligibility smarter and more efficient.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So whether you're a fiscal conservative concerned about government efficiency or a progressive that's concerned about access to benefits, there's something here that we should all be able to embrace.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And as we discuss housing affordability in general today, including a lot of the great bills.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: that we're hearing.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Let's remember that keeping New Yorkers in the homes they already own is every bit as important as creating new housing opportunities.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Nobody should be taxed out of their home because they failed a paperwork test rather than an income tax.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So I'm looking forward to hearing what everybody has to say on it, and I respectfully urge my colleagues on both committees to support this resolution.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Sanchez acknowledges Councilmember Maloney and asks for Councilmember Joseph, then turns to committee counsel to administer the oath to the administration witnesses.
chapters.title: Sanchez transitions to administration testimony, administers oath

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Morano.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Now, Councilmember Maloney.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Is here.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And Councilmember Joseph?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Well, with all of that preamble, I would now like to turn it over to our committee counsel to administer the oath.

chapters.title: Committee counsel administers oath to administration witnesses

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Please raise your right hand.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Do you affirm to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth before this committee, and to respond honestly to council member questions?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Adolfo Carrión Jr., HPD Commissioner, introduces himself and shares his background in housing, including work at UHAB, the Attorney General's office, and HCR. He states the administration's commitment to preserving and expanding homeownership opportunities.
chapters.title: HPD Commissioner Carrión testifies on administration's homeownership commitment

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Good morning, Chair Sanchez and Chair Lee and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Thank you for having me here today.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: I'm very happy to be here and especially pleased to be talking with you about the administration's commitment to preserving and expanding homeownership opportunities across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: As I've shared in past testimony, advancing avenues to preserve and create more homeownership has been central throughout my career.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Working to expand limited equity cooperatives during my 10 years at UHAB, combating deed theft and foreclosure abuses during my time at the Attorney General's office,

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: and leading the state's mortgage agency, homeowner resiliency programs, and new homeownership production work during my time at HCR.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Affordable homeownership gives New Yorkers the opportunity to build equity, preserve generational wealth, and achieve greater agency over the space in which they live.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: It is a key feature of Mayor Mondani's housing plan, Block by Block, which calls for a significant expansion of HPD programs dedicated to making affordable homeownership more accessible to low- and moderate-income New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: This is particularly true with regard to serving New Yorkers who have systematically been denied

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: access to homeownership historically due to redlining and other racist housing policy.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: The rate of homeownership among black and brown New Yorkers has fallen significantly in the last two decades, with effects of both the foreclosure crisis and COVID disproportionately impacting these communities.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: That is unacceptable, and we are committed to changing it.

chapters.summary: Carrión describes HPD's dual strategy: preserving homeownership for existing residents and expanding access for new buyers. He details the Office of the Homeowner Advocate, the Homeowner Handbook, the Homeownership Help Desk, and programs like Home Fix, Flood Help NY, and estate planning.
chapters.title: Carrión outlines HPD's two pillars and Office of Homeowner Advocate services

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: HPD approaches our work in this space through a commitment to two pillars, preserving homeownership for existing residents and expanding access and supply for New Yorkers who are striving to achieve this opportunity, in many cases for the first time.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: When it comes to supporting homeowners, HPD oversees a broad suite of programs, many of which fall under the auspices of the Office of the Homeowner Advocate.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Established in 2023 thanks to legislation sponsored by Councilmember Brooks Powers and passed by the full council, this office provides an array of services to support existing homeowners.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: The office publishes the Homeowner Handbook, which is a comprehensive guide for homeowners, including information on how to access all of HPD's programs, as well as resources provided by our partners, including legal services and housing counseling agencies.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: It is now available in nine languages, and in fiscal year 2026,

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: The web version of this handbook was accessed over 6,000 times.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: In the fall of 2024, HPD worked with the Center for New York City Neighborhoods, now the Center for New York City Neighborhoods,

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: for New York Homeownership to launch the citywide Homeownership Help Desk, which serves as a one-stop shop for homeowners in need of assistance.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: The Help Desk connects homeowners to an ever-growing number of programs, including the Home Fix Program, which provides grants for urgent home repairs and to support resiliency improvements for low- and moderate-income homeowners.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: To housing counseling and legal services for homeowners who are at risk of mortgage default and foreclosure.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Flood Help NY, through which homeowners receive access to free resiliency audits, education on flood preparedness, and financial counseling dedicated to making sure homeowners are better protected in the face of rising climate threats.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: And referrals to the Estate Planning and Resolution Initiative to support homeowners who are at high risk of deed theft or who are navigating issues with regard to airship rights and other complex title transactions.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Each of these services are provided to homeowners free of charge, and in 2026 alone, more than 8,400 households received assistance.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Finally, HPD has added $2 million in annual dedicated funding to support outreach and counseling to ensure that homeowners who are impacted by past

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: or future tax lien sales have access to loss mitigation and foreclosure prevention services.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: HPD shares the goals of Intro 1096 and appreciates the sponsors.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: leadership on this issue.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: We would like the opportunity to discuss the proposed legislation and how it relates to the work already being executed by the Office of the Homeowner Advocate.

chapters.summary: Carrión mentions the $7 million UHAB contract for HDFC training and technical assistance, reaching thousands of cooperators. He also notes a new RFP for Mitchell Lama co-ops and shares goals of Intro 406 to strengthen support for co-ops.
chapters.title: Carrión discusses HDFC training contract and Intro 406 goals

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: In addition to these individual services, HPD is committed to ensuring that New York City's large stock of shared equity cooperatives have access to critical financial and governance support through our HDFC training and technical assistance contract.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Managed by the Urban Homesteading Assistance Board, this $7 million program provides free technical assistance, training, and financial counseling to co-op boards.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: and to existing shareholders.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: The program reaches thousands of cooperators every year.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Additionally, HPD has just released a request for proposals to identify technical assistance providers to support Mitchell Lama co-ops, who also need assistance with governance and with preparing applications to HPD and HDC

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: for capital improvement financing.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: HPD plans to launch this new initiative in the first quarter of 2027.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: With respect to Intro 406, we share the goals of this bill and look forward to working with the sponsors to identify how we can best strengthen support for co-ops based on the existing programs I've already described.

chapters.summary: Carrión outlines plans to double Open Door production to 300 units annually, launch the Our Home program to convert rentals to limited equity co-ops (150 units/year), and expand Home First down payment assistance to 300 homebuyers by FY2028.
chapters.title: Carrión details Open Door, Our Home, and Home First expansion plans

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Shifting to our second pillar of homeownership work, the administration has committed significant resources to create and expand access to affordable homeownership as outlined in Block by Block.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: First is our commitment to expand the Open Door Program, our primary tool for financing new construction of affordable homeownership units.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: The program will aim to double our production in fiscal year 27 and 28 to produce 300 units annually.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: We are also preparing to launch our newest program, Our Home, which is the first time since the creation of the third-party transfer program that HPD has had a dedicated turn sheet to convert existing rental buildings into limited equity cooperatives.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Under this new program, HPD estimates that we will be able to convert 150 units per year over the

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: the next two years.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: And finally, we have committed to a significant expansion of Home First, HPD's down payment assistance program for low and moderate income households.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: These $100,000 forgivable grants are critical to ensuring that New York has access to existing homeownership markets.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: In fiscal year 2026, the program served roughly 170 homebuyers.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Our ambitious expansion will scale up to reach a target of at least 300 prospective homebuyers in fiscal year 2028.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: However, it is important to acknowledge that while down payment assistance is extremely important, challenges with expanding this program are driven by current market conditions,

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: including rising mortgage rates and escalating operating costs, which increase the monthly maintenance and HOA fees that prospective homebuyers must pay once they've purchased a home.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: While HPD fully supports increasing down payment assistance, with regard to Intro 862, we would like to work with the bill sponsors to discuss how these market conditions impact short-term expansion efforts.

chapters.summary: Carrión discusses challenges with the Housing Choice Voucher Homeownership Program, including the 15-year voucher cliff and payment standards not adjusting to market rates. He expresses willingness to work on Intro 1082 and 861 to overcome barriers.
chapters.title: Carrión addresses HCV homeownership barriers and related bills

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Now I'd like to take a moment to discuss similar market barriers that affect our past and current efforts to assist households receiving housing choice vouchers with conversion to homeownership.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: HPD believes that this program presents tremendous opportunity for many low-income New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Through our Housing Access and Stability Division, there is a dedicated team at HPD who perform outreach, training, and technical assistance to our Housing Choice Voucher recipients.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: who may be eligible for this program.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Currently, there are over 160 voucher holders working with HPD to participate.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: The HCV homeownership program is governed by federal rules, some of which make higher utilization rates difficult to achieve.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: One rule stipulates that users of this program must give up their voucher at the end of the 15th year of the program.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: As most mortgages are based on a 30-year amortization schedule, participants in this program therefore face a fiscal cliff that may lead to mortgage default or foreclosure risk once they reach year 15.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Second, the payment standard for housing choice vouchers under the program do not adjust to reflect rising mortgage interest rates or the increases in monthly maintenance HOA fees as previously discussed.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: As a result, voucher holders struggle to find homes for purchase where monthly payments fit within the Section 8 payment standard.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Despite these challenges, we will continue to work towards making this program more effective and would be happy to work with the sponsors of Intro 1082

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: and Intro 861 to identify pathways to overcome some of the barriers to expanding utilization of this program.

chapters.summary: Carrión reports that the Land Bank Board has begun meeting and aims to submit an application to the state in early 2027. The bank will prioritize minimizing disparate impacts and foreclosure prevention, with public hearings planned.
chapters.title: Carrión updates on NYC Land Bank formation and goals

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Finally, I would like to update the Council on the progress that HPD and our public and private partners have advanced in recent months with regard to standing up the New York City Land Bank.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: The seven-member Board of Directors, including Council and mayoral appointees and ex officio members, including myself,

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: have begun meeting regularly, and we are on track to have an application ready to present to the state in early 2027.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: We have also begun to articulate the goals and the mission of the land bank with an emphasis on minimizing disparate impacts on low-income residents in black and brown communities and prioritizing homeownership retention and foreclosure prevention wherever possible.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: In early to mid-2027, the Land Bank Board will publish bylaws and hold a public hearing to solicit feedback from stakeholders.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: And we look forward to briefing members of this Council as we make progress towards establishing this important preservation vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Again, I would like to thank the Council for calling this important hearing on a broad range of topics related to homeownership.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: As I have said, it is an issue that is of great importance to me personally and to the administration.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: We look forward to working with members of the Council to continue to find ways to make homeownership a reality for more New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Thank you for this opportunity to testify, and I look forward to answering your questions.

chapters.summary: Sanchez thanks Commissioner Carrión and asks if DOB will read their testimony. After some confusion, she acknowledges that everyone will just read it.
chapters.title: Sanchez thanks Carrión, calls for DOB testimony

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Is DOB going to read your testimony as well?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: All right, everybody just read it.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: There you go.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: There you go.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Well, thank you so much, Commissioner and members of the administration for being here and participating today.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm going to ask just a few questions to start and turn it over to Chair Lee.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Excuse me, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: I have testimony.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Oh, you do?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: See, I knew something was missing.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Deputy Commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Go ahead.

chapters.summary: Jeffrey Shear, First Deputy Commissioner of DOF, expresses concerns about Intro 1084, which would automatically enroll delinquent property owners in payment plans. He cites operational challenges, lack of owner information, potential confusion, and suggests an opt-in approach instead.
chapters.title: DOF First Deputy Commissioner Shear testifies against Intro 1084

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Before you begin, I want to acknowledge that we're joined by Councilmember Mealy.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Good morning, Chair Sanchez, Chair Lee, and members of the two committees.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: I am Jeffrey Shear, the first Deputy Commissioner of the Department of Finance, and I am joined today by Deputy Commissioner Annette Hill.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: I would like to thank the Council for giving me the opportunity to testify before you today about Introduction 1084.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: DOF appreciates the Council's interest in helping homeowners manage their property tax obligations and recognizes the financial challenges that property taxes can present for certain households, particularly seniors,

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: individuals on fixed incomes, and homeowners experiencing financial hardship.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: But we do have concerns about the bill.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Introduction 1084 would require the department to automatically enroll delinquent property tax owners in a city-created property tax payment plan that requires them to pay the lowest total amount.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: DOF offers six different property tax payment plans and has a rigorous program to notify owners of their availability through our property tax bills, notices of property value,

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: delinquency notices, and tax lien sale communications, as well as our website and numerous outreach events.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Imposing payment plans without the consent of delinquents.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: owners and without required information pertaining to the owner's age, income,

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: residency status, and size, or especially the age of their debt, may cause confusion and distrust and also may lead to a variety of negative outcomes.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: While selecting a plan based on the lowest total cost may sound straightforward, a payment plan necessarily increases the interest charges owed by the owner.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Owners with lower, newer debt and with sufficient assets who plan on paying the debt in the near future

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: will face their lowest cost by paying in full and not entering into a payment plan, which can extend for multiple years.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: For owners with larger debts and who cannot pay, DOF must know their age, income, and residency status to determine if they qualify for payment plans with lower interest,

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: such as our PTAID and reduced interest plans.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Without that information, we have no way of assigning them to the lowest cost option.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: In addition, we need the owner's input to determine the desired length of a payment plan.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Longer plans have lower installment payments but accrue more interest over time.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Furthermore, mandating a plan could have the unintended consequence of expediting enforcement action against the

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Owners who default on a payment plan can only get a lifeline payment plan with a 20% down payment for five years after the default.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: It may be best to consider this type of dramatic action for owners who are in a tax lien sale at-risk pool.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Another issue with the bill is the advance notification section.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: It requires DOF to provide notice of automatic enrollment at least 60 days before the first payment is due.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Although advance notification is usually desirable, the proposed approach could cause confusion among property owners

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: who receive notices indicating that they have been enrolled in a payment plan that they did not affirmatively request.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Taxpayers may mistakenly believe that enrollment is mandatory, that their property status has changed, that they have incurred a new financial obligation,

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: or that an unauthorized third party has made a commitment without their consent.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Implementing Introduction 1084 would require DOF to develop, maintain, and continuously update an automated enrollment system capable of identifying eligible

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: individuals, and determining the applicable lowest cost payment plan.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: This would involve substantial operation coordination and technological development, including establishing

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: establishing eligibility criteria across different payment plan programs, developing automated processes to calculate and compare the total cost of available plans,

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: establishing and maintaining an accessible opt-out mechanism, and providing multilingual communications in designated citywide languages.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: For DOF, this is operationally a very heavy lift that would require more staff and technology updates to existing systems.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: For these reasons, the Department of Finance cannot support Introduction 1094 in its current form.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: The Department shares the Council's objective of helping New Yorkers manage their property tax obligations and ensuring that eligible homeowners are aware of available payment plan options.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: We look forward to engaging with the Council on constructive conversations about Introduction 1084.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: We welcome the opportunity to work with the Council on approaches that improve access to property tax payment options while protecting taxpayers and ensuring the efficient administration of the City's property tax system.

chapters.summary: Sanchez thanks Shear for his testimony. Carrión introduces Michael Sandler, Deputy Commissioner for the Office of Neighborhood Services, which oversees the Office of the Homeowner Advocate.
chapters.title: Sanchez thanks Shear; Carrión introduces Deputy Commissioner Sandler

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much, First Deputy Commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Yes, Commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Sorry, I was very remiss not to introduce my colleague, Michael Sandler, who is our Deputy Commissioner for the...

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Office of Neighborhood Services, which oversees the Office of the Homeowner Advocate.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Michael Sandler is a star here, so thank you for being with us.

chapters.summary: Sanchez acknowledges Councilmember Shirley Aldebo on Zoom and says she will ask a few questions before turning to co-chair Lee and other colleagues.
chapters.title: Sanchez acknowledges Councilmember Aldebo, starts Q&A

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Before we begin questions, I just want to acknowledge that we're joined on Zoom by Councilmember Shirley Aldebo.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So as I said, I will ask a few, turn it over to my co-chair and then colleagues as well.

chapters.summary: Sanchez asks what makes this administration's approach different and what the overarching goals are. Carrión explains the dual strategy of preventing loss of existing homes and increasing homeownership through new programs like Our Home and Home First.
chapters.title: Sanchez asks Carrión how administration's homeownership approach differs

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So first, the administration's housing plan outlines several new initiatives to expand access to homeownership.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The Our Home program, which you discussed, to convert rentals into resident-controlled co-ops, a preservation pre-development fund for HDFC co-ops, transferring land to community land trusts to create one-to-four family homeownership opportunities, and more.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So my first question is a big picture question.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: What makes this administration's approach to homeownership different from past administrations?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: What are the overarching goals behind the new initiatives that you are launching?

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Thank you for the question.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: I would say, to kind of go back to what I said in my testimony, I think the administration is very focused on sort of a dual strategy as it relates to homeownership.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: The first, as we heard about from some of the members, is making sure that folks who already have achieved that are not at risk of losing their homes or that they are not being subjected to predatory practices, which we know are just gaining steam.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: So I think there is a really deep effort to making sure that

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Folks, and particularly, as I said, underserved communities, are not losing the wealth and the generational assets that they've achieved through homeownership.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Secondarily, I think there is a big push in this housing plan, as you saw, which maybe has been lacking in previous...

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: whatever, decades, to really increase the amount of homeownership that exists in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: And there's really two ways that we're approaching that.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: The first is increasing access by increasing the number of units that we finance or that we convert through programs like Our Home.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Again, this is the first time, I think, since I got to New York City that HPD has had a term sheet dedicated specifically to converting in-place rental buildings into homeownership.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: And then the second is creating more market access, which primarily we do through our down payment program called Home First.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: They're happy we'll talk about it, I'm sure, some challenges in the current market environment that we're in today.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Again, rising interest rates and rising property costs.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Insurance taxes is making it more and more difficult, even with a very generous down payment assistance product, to get folks into the sort of private market of homeownership.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: That said, I think we have been scaling up Home First, and we have made a very serious commitment to keep scaling it up.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: And we are also looking forward to working with our partners at the state, where I used to work, including with the state of New York mortgage agency, Sunny May, where I

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: see real opportunity to sort of marry some of our offerings and the state's offerings to try to overcome some of the market barriers.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Commissioner.

chapters.summary: Sanchez asks about funding committed to Our Home in FY27 and 28, share prices, and monthly maintenance targets. Carrión says term sheet coming soon, targeting 50-120% AMI, and $75 million in capital budget for two years.
chapters.title: Sanchez questions Carrión on Our Home funding and AMI targets

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Speaking of our home, you mentioned in your testimony and, of course, in the plan, it is stated the goal of achieving 300 units across fiscal years 2027 and 2028.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Can you share with us how much funding is committed to our home in the fiscal 27 and 28 budgets?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: What share price and monthly maintenance levels is HPD targeting?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Your testimony mentions that HPD is preparing to launch our home.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: When will you release the term sheet for the new program?

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: So we are very optimistic that the term sheet will be out very soon, if not by the end of the year, then certainly in early, early days in calendar year 2027.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Because we have not finalized the term sheet, I can give you broad stroke outlines of how I think the term sheet will sort of work in terms of AMIs and how we're targeting that.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Generally speaking, because these will be in-place tenants and because there can be a range of incomes in private buildings, we're going to have a fairly broad spectrum of who the program will serve.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Probably at the low end, we'll be looking at folks who can afford at 50% AMI and probably at the upper end, including outsiders who will purchase vacant units in these buildings, up to about 120% AMI.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: Again, I want to sort of just remind you that the term sheet isn't yet finalized, but that's sort of...

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: the shape we're expecting it to take.

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: As to the budget, there's about $75 million included in our capital budget for both

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: two years, for the two years, in order to finance the conversion and the rehab that we anticipate will be necessary as we're helping tenants convert their buildings.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I missed the number.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: How much?

utterances.speaker: Adolfo Carrión Jr.
utterances.text: $75 million.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: $75 million.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Commissioner.

chapters.summary: Sanchez asks why a lien sale is necessary in 2027 after suspension in 2026, and what outreach funding is committed. Shear explains reforms, including raising foreclosure minimum to $70,000, connecting homeowners to resources, and increasing water/sewer debt threshold.
chapters.title: Sanchez questions DOF on 2027 lien sale and outreach plans

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And my next question is on the lien sale.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The city has historically used a tax lien sale to recover unpaid property taxes, water and sewage bills, and certain charges for repairs.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The administration suspended the lien sale in 2026 for review of the program, but it has since been reported that the administration will conduct a lien sale in mid-2027.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: As you can imagine, there are lots of my colleagues here for whom that is very alarming as their homeowners, the homeowners in their district, are already facing a lot of pressures.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So first, why did the administration determine that a lien sale was not necessary in 2026 but will be necessary in 2027?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And important to us, how much funding is committed to outreach for affected homeowners?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: What specific strategies will the administration take to ensure as many homeowners as possible are able to resolve their debts prior to a lien sale?

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: So over the last six months, we've used the pause in the lien sale to conduct a rigorous assessment of our cities of the lien sale process.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: As the city works to set up the New York City Land Bank, this administration's restructuring

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: on top of previous reform efforts, has worked to create a fundamentally different lien sale outreach process that is rooted in intensive outreach to protect homeowners,

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: compassionate resolution, and multiple opportunities to avoid the sale of the lien against the property.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: The City is introducing several reforms for 2027 to help homeowners resolve outstanding debts before their properties enter the lien sale,

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: strengthen protections, expand payment options, and improve enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: The major reforms include

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Raising the foreclosure minimum for our owner-occupied tax class one properties to $70,000 or more than 15% of the property's market value.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: This addresses concerns about homeowners potentially losing their properties through foreclosure over relatively small amounts of debt.

utterances.speaker: Jeffrey Shear
utterances.text: Connecting homeowners who use the easy exit feature during the 2020.
