utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: And I'm blind and low vision, so I'm going to summarize just a few points and we'll follow up in writing with our full testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: In that note, I want to start with the senior and disability exemption.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: It is our, you know,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: perspective to support streamlining and making that program much simpler.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: Somebody like me who is blind is not going to be blind.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: It's not going to stop being blind because I didn't certify for my tax exemption the next year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: Just as a senior is not going to stop being a senior because I didn't get the right paperwork in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: So we encourage that program to be streamlined and move forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: I also stand with my colleague from UHAB in supporting renewing the damp tax cap.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: Habitat has a CDFI, the Habitat New York City Community Fund, in which we support through our housing preservation program and through the fund HDFC cooperatives in preserving their affordability and staying stable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: Financing is very difficult when there is no damp caps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: Tax cap promised moving forward after 2029.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: So we support the reform to that program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: And I also wanted to just highlight one thing on the voucher, the homeownership voucher conversions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: We support any

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: all efforts to advance vouchers being utilized for affordable homeownership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: And I want to emphasize that NYCHA actually currently does not participate in the program in the same way that the other programs do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: And that is something that the city council and the city should take on to make sure that NYCHA is also utilizing the homeownership voucher program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: And lastly, I also want to mention that we are extremely supportive and happy that the council

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: is so robustly behind increasing the stock of affordable homeownership, including the open door program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: And there were so many great questions around conversion opportunities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: So I just also wanted to emphasize that while our home is a great start with 300 units, there are hundreds of buildings and tens of thousands of tenants that would love to convert their homes to home ownership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: And we partner with those organizations or with those tenants and landlords.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: And so we would love to see those programs expand so that we can utilize year 15, year 30 light tech conversions, rent stabilized tenants that want to become homeowners,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: Affordable Housing Retention Act, cooperative conversions, and many other ways that we can expand tenant opportunities to purchase and see more tenants become homeowners in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Lee asks Ariel Hirsch about HPD enforcement capacity for HDFCs, and Bradley McCormick about how the city can help homeowners while avoiding predatory scams from the lien sale list. Hirsch says HPD lacks tools; McCormick says the public list is a problem.
chapters.title: Lee asks panel about HPD enforcement and lien sale alternatives

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Just really quick questions for a couple of you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So for Ariel, quick question, because on the enforcement piece, not to make assumptions, but were you...

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: saying that HPD should be the one to enforce or?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: Yeah, so I think that what a lot of HDFC shareholders experience is when they have an issue in their building, they will go and try to resolve it internally.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: They'll reach out to UHAB.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: And if they reach an impasse and they need HPD to step in for illegal subletting practices or financial mismanagement or lack of transparency that other efforts have been unable to resolve,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: HPD often does not have the capacity and the tools to step in, especially in those ways that are dealing with individual shareholder issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: They have regulatory authority for buildings that have regulatory agreements, but the vast majority, about 1,000 out of 1,200 HDFC co-ops, have no agreement on the books with HPD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: And this means that there's a gap in their ability to step in when there are serious issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: You have this also a monitor for some buildings with regulatory agreements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: And even in those instances where HPD does have the authority through their regulatory agreement to step in, it is still very difficult

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: to get members of HPD to actually act and be able to use that enforcement capacity.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, thank you for clarifying that.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And then just also really quickly for Bradley, and I'm sorry if it's in your testimony, I haven't had a chance to read the whole thing, but I totally hear you and folks in this room I think would agree that

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: with the incoming, you know, lien sale and it leading to d-theft and being predatory and scams,

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: how would you suggest the city go about making sure that we are helping homeowners to alleviate their issues?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Obviously, in my opinion, that should be the first step is to not foreclose, but obviously help them to fix whatever issues that they're dealing with.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And so how would you sort of couple?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Allowing the city to be able to help them versus, you know, keeping the list, you know, not public in terms of having it go to scams and being predatory.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bradley McCormick
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bradley McCormick
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to speak out of turn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bradley McCormick
utterances.text: I don't really have an answer to that off the top of my head, but I do think that the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bradley McCormick
utterances.text: The public nature of the list is a problem, and it gives scammers an opportunity to basically counter the city's outreach with outreach of their own.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And if any of you all have creative thoughts on that, I would love to hear it because I think the best ideas come from the community themselves.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And so if there are creative ways where we can think through that, I would love to hear it in the future.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And I'm sure Chair Sanchez would too.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you all.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, next up we have Martha Sickles, David Calvert.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Brixby Esbelde, sorry if I'm mispronouncing, and Gloria Ann Kirsten.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Yes, and you can go in whatever order.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: You don't have to do it in the name order that I called.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, and begin when ready.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: You got, oh, you just have to push the button.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: There you go.

chapters.summary: David Calvert, an HDFC shareholder since 1980, supports extending the DAMP tax abatement but asks for protections for future shareholders. He urges adding language to Resolution 9 to keep sales prices moderate and ensure future generations can benefit.
chapters.title: David Calvert testifies for future HDFC shareholders

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: My name is David Calvert.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: I'm an HDFC shareholder since 1980.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: And, you know, building we squatted and then till and then became legal 43 years ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: And I love my building and I'm sure everybody who's ever lived in HDFC shares some of that feeling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: I'm here to speak for...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: AHIFA, which is Affordable Housing is for All, and our name says exactly what we stand for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: And I think that everybody in the room will probably agree that the damp tax abatement needs to be extended.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: We're all for that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: But get into the weeds on some other issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: And I think you're going to hear a lot of testimony today about too much government oversight on the buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: And you're going to hear a lot of testimony about not having control of sales and let's see.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: Sales just sort of go.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: People may not be saying that, but that's in the weeds there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: And I'm here to stand for the people who are not in the building, who are not yet identified, but who are the next shareholders in these buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: Next year, future generations, we need to come up with some rules in the state legislation that's being proposed that protect future shareholders, not just the rights of current shareholders, but the future.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: That's my plea.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: The people that came up like I did, needing housing so badly in 1980, those young people are still coming up and they are still going to need housing, and we need to find a way to make sure that happens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: So I say for Resolution 9, add some language that says we support this bill at the state level, but we want some protections to keep those sales prices

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: moderate and keep them not inflated and make sure that future shareholders can come in and get the same benefits we got.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Calvert
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Gloria Ann Kerstein, an HDFC shareholder for 33 years, describes her building's low maintenance due to DAMP, self-management, and flip tax. She notes intergenerational transfers and asks HPD to invite the HDFC Coalition to the table for discussions.
chapters.title: Gloria Ann Kerstein describes her HDFC's affordability and intergenerational transfers

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: I'm Gloria Ann Kerstein.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: I have been an HDFC shareholder on West 106th Street for 33 years in a building where I've lived for 44 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: I would like to readdress the problem of affordability to have protection be paramount for the HDFC shareholders already living in HDFC co-ops.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: I'd like to paint a portrait of my own particular HDFC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: We're in an old law tenement five-story walk-up built in 1885, which is typical of almost all of the HDFCs in Manhattan, Williamsburg, and the like.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: And the portrait that I want to convey includes the fact that for the past 33 years, we have had only four sales.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: Because our maintenance is so low.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: Rentals on West 106 for a one-bedroom range between $3,200 and $3,900 per month.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: A one-bedroom in my HDFC is $736 maintenance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: Because we have the damp tax protection.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: Secondly, we're self-managed, which is a real challenge more and more each year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: And thirdly, we're...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: And we do have a sale.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: We have a robust flip tax that can help our income stream meet the expenses that mount majorly year by year, such as insurance and oil, which we're all familiar with.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: Among the HDFC shareholders that originally incorporated in 1993 in my building, seven have passed on, and in every case, all seven shares went to their children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: So we didn't have any sales.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: So we have had intergenerational transfer in these 33 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: Among those of us who remain, we're a NORC, naturally occurring retirement community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: Six of us are seniors, including myself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: And why do we stay here?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: Because it's affordable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: So the Resolution 9 is important.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: I have one more very important thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: The bill that's in Albany was crafted by the HDFC Coalition over five arduous years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: We're the ones, we're volunteers, we're the ones that came up with the bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: But we have yet to be invited to the table by HPD Commissioner Levy, who is here today saying she had discussions with the lawmakers, but not with those of us who made this bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: So we welcome an invitation from HPD to bring us to the table.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gloria Ann Kerstein
utterances.text: We're the ones who live in these buildings and whose homeownership and affordability is at threat.

chapters.summary: Martha Sickles, urban planner and HDFC Coalition member, supports the intent of Resolution 9 but asks for a forum with HPD and stakeholders. She suggests percentage reductions instead of valuation caps, a 120% AMI cap, and better data collection.
chapters.title: Martha Sickles suggests amendments to Resolution 9 for equity and oversight

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Lee and committee members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: Thank you for holding this homeownership oversight hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: I'm Martha Sickles, an urban planner, member of the HIPAA Coalition, Green Co-op Council, and chairholder in HDFC Co-op.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: I support the intent of the bills and resolutions on the agenda to improve and expand affordable homeownership programs and protections, increase public education and awareness, and improve administration of tax abatements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: I appreciate the spirit of Resolution 9 to extend the damp tax exemption,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: but the HDFC Fairness Preservation Affordability Act, as drafted, is potentially inconsistent with city policy and fails to adequately address affordability equity

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: and adequate oversight of the damp tax abatement program for all HDFCs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: I ask you to, as many of my colleagues have, to facilitate a forum with HPD, state elected officials,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: HDFC representatives, and other stakeholders to improve the legislation to best meet the challenges of the city's affordability crisis and HDFCs as housing costs escalate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: The extension has been under discussion for many years, as noted, and there's still time for the state legislation to get it right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: Please consider three key elements, equity, affordability, and adequate oversight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: HDFC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: HTFCs in lower-income neighborhoods do not benefit from proposed valuation caps and would be better addressed with percentage reductions or another formula.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: Article 11 of the 1966 Private Housing Finance Law requires HTFCs to provide housing for low-income families, citing an income limit of 165% of AMI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: With changing income demographics, this AMI is considered a higher income tier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: 120% of AMI is considered moderate to middle income, a more appropriate income level cap.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: It's crucial to keep HDFCs affordable for future generations, as noted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: And HPD must be able to collect and evaluate HDFCs and the whole management of these buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: So adequate compliance is important as well as to collect data on sales price trends.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martha Sickles
utterances.text: I thank you for the opportunity to testify and offer the assistance of our organizations to create a representative forum to discuss these issues and design improved legislation.

chapters.summary: Brixby Appelty, board president of a 24-unit HDFC in Hamilton Heights, describes challenges for lower-income buyers and the need for resale price protections. She urges amendments to Resolution 9 to keep opportunity open for all income levels.
chapters.title: Brixby Appelty testifies on affordability and income limits in HDFCs

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: Thank you for this opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: I'm Brixby Appelty and a Haifa member, shareholder, and board president of a 24-unit HDFC in Hamilton Heights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: Generations of New Yorkers fought and continue to fight for HDFCs, making my home ownership possible today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: DAMP helps sustain this, and we are responsible for keeping it available to the next family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: But affordability does not preserve itself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: In my building, that responsibility means reckoning with some hard questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: Could my neighbors afford to buy into the co-op today?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: Could their children?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: Could some shareholders afford to, but not others?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: Long-term shareholders in my building share a two-bedroom apartment across three generations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: Their adult children want homes in their own building where they grew up and can't afford a $300,000 two-bedroom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: And at 92% AMI myself, my family can't afford a larger unit, so our $200,000 one-bedroom can't open up for another family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: That's why Resolution 9 matters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: The bill would let HDFCs raise existing lower income limits to 165% AMI once city-imposed restrictions end.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: Once resale price protections, or without resale price protections, the bill leaves lower income families competing for homes priced toward higher income purchasers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: Even home first isn't always available.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: to HDFC buyers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: We had a tenant at 70% AMI with an approved loan and home first qualification, but our building's low owner occupancy made us ineligible for a conventional financing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: And therefore, home first was unavailable to us and the buyer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: So the bill gives greater tax relief to higher valued buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brixby Appelty
utterances.text: A roof costs no less in the Bronx than in Manhattan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And any board will tell you a tax cap reduces what a building owes, but it doesn't pay the bills.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Finally, the bill relies on self-certification without public data on sale prices or purchase or incomes or city verification.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: How can shareholders or lawmakers verify compliance or challenge violations without that information?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Accountability must be cooperative, self-governance, not replace or...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Not replace or burden it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I urge you to amend Resolution 9 and keep the opportunity open for everyone.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Great, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And I just want to echo the fact that, you know, the intergenerational piece is super important that I don't think folks recognize enough, and especially in my areas of Queens, especially Southeast Queens,

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: a lot of the black, brown, Asian communities, that really is so, but what ends up happening is because of all the high costs and loans and everything, they end up

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: being maybe having a great asset but cash poor.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And so we have to make sure that we're preventing a lot of these homeowners from defaulting or getting into foreclosure.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So you gave a lot of really good recommendations, the 165 AMI.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And if there are other ideas and suggestions you have that are not in here, please feel free to include that in your testimony when you submit it.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Because I tell you this for everyone in the room, the staff here read every single word and actually incorporate that a lot of times into

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: the bill amendments that we're working on.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So we appreciate any and all feedback.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So thank you all so much.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Linda Lee calls the next panel. Sabrina Lam, speaking for the Harlem Coalition, describes seniors facing property tax increases from $14 to over $900 per month as 421A abatements expire. She asks the council to adopt Resolution 9, expand it to HPD buildings, and pass Resolution 599.
chapters.title: Panel called: Cherise Terrain, Sabrina Lam, Morris Lundy, Louis Clark; Sabrina Lam testifies on 421A expirations

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, next up we have Cherise Terrain, Sabrina Lam, Morris Lundy, and Louis Clark.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Sorry, Louise, not Louis.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I can't read.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: My eyes are fading.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, and feel free to start in whichever order you would like.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Good afternoon and thank you for this hearing today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: If any city council committee can get this done, I believe that you all will and can together with us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: My name is Sabrina Lam and I speak for the Harlem Coalition for Age and Place and Affordable Dignity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: We live in an HDC regulated co-op at East Harlem and we have submitted our full written testimony with letters of support from community boards 9, 10, and 11.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: The families who

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: built Harlem are being taxed out of it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: As the Wall Street Journal reported, when our neighbor, Audrey Henry, bought her home in 2004, buyers were promised a new program before the abatement ran out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Don't worry about it, she was told, and others were told.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Now our 421 abatements are expiring, and the law taxes are only homes like an investment property.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Meet also my neighbor, Ruth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: She's 80 years old on a fixed income and has lived in her co-op for more than 20 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Her property tax was $14 a month, and now it's going up to over $900.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: This is not a budget increase.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: It's an eviction notice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: And 47% of our residents are in Ruth's position.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: The cliff has already set a trap.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: One neighbor can't afford to stay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Another can't afford to leave because our resale prices are restricted by design while our costs now move with the market.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: And Ruth is not alone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: The Roebling Index found that over 160,000 New York City apartments are losing 421A benefits between 2023 and 2040.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: And about 25,000 households in limited equity co-ops and condos face this cliff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Disproportionately Black and Latino communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Community boards 9, 10, and 11.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: have all affirmatively called for action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: And so we asked the council for three things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: First, adopt Resolution 009, which calls on New York State to pass the Jackson-Taylor HGC-FC Act and also amend it to include HPD buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: And we fully support that state bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Second, expand it to include HGC-regulated co-ops like ours and call for a transition relief that pauses these increases while Albany acts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Without that amendment, everyone, our homes are left out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: And third, adopt Resolution 0599 so seniors can stop losing tax relief they qualify for because of paperwork.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Harlem and the Harlems of New York City is not for sale.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Please help the people who built it so we can age in place and affordable dignity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Cherise Terrain, founder of the Black Homeowners Preservation Coalition, describes her family being victims of a deed scam two weeks ago. She asks to strengthen Intro 1096 with immediate screening for deed theft complaints, enforceable deadlines, and trauma-informed practices.
chapters.title: Cherise Terrain testifies on deed theft and need for stronger protections

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair and Council Members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: I am Cherise Terrain, a student at Columbia MSW program, founder

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: and executive director of the Black Homeowners Preservation Coalition, founder and architect of the Stop D Theft Movement, co-founder of Women of the Stop D Theft Movement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: At 964 Parplace, my family has lived for over 75 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: And unfortunately, just two weeks ago, we were victims of a legal fraud deed scam to throw us out of our home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: And we experienced the consequences of fighting for ownership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: While facing this illegal removal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: This has affected my mental health, my reproductive health, financial security, safety, family stability, and quality of life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: My grandmother was born in the Jim Crow South, but unfortunately she died in this New York City Jim Crow North.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: So therefore, we come here today, myself and some of my congrats, and we're asking to strengthen Intro 1096.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: We require immediate screening for every D-theft complaint for RPAPL 756A protection.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: an immediate agency action for every homeowner who meets the statutory conditions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Require a name coordinating agency, enforceable emergency response deadlines, written decisions, and full-scope legal assistance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Mandate a trauma-informed practice, culturally competence, and culturally humility under a racial equity framework that recognizes the history of Black dispossession.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: My forum funnel, which I will give to the committee, analyzes the identities, identifies the identities of danger homeownership faces when you are dispossessed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: I will, can I have one more minute?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Sorry, okay.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Oh yeah, you can just wrap up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Okay, wrap up, okay, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: We required a public privacy protection for black specific outcome reporting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Possession, was asking questions like, was possession preserved?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Was title restored?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Was equity recovered?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: How about health, safety, inheritance, family stability protected?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: We don't need any more referrals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: We need protection.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Was it a full investigation?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Not just asking a question about investigation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Did we get restoration?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Was there a temporary stay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Or was title restored?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: That's what we're asking.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: We're asking for full protection of a family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Protective family, protective quality of life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Because black.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Betts died.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: It's no longer black.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: And we are not getting full protection.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Our seniors are losing not just their homes, but their life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cherise Terrain
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Morris Lundy, a Section 8 voucher holder from Far Rockaway, was told the HCV homeownership program didn't exist. He asks for clear rules and accurate information, and also complains about poor Section 8 inspections that let substandard units pass.
chapters.title: Morris Lundy testifies on HCV homeownership misinformation and inspections

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: Hello, committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: My name is Morris Lundy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: I'm a HPD Section 8 participant at Far Rockaway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: I previously asked Section 8 about the homeownership voucher, and I was told that it didn't exist.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: But after research, I found that Chapter 20 of the HPD's April 2025 administrative plan described the housing choice voucher option.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: The conflicting information prevented us from finding out what steps we needed to move forward with having our voucher converted over into a homeownership program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: I'm asking the council to basically require HBD to publish clear rules of eligibility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: Enrollment status, application instructions, designation, home ownership contact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: Staff should explain whether the program is unavailable, closed to enrollment, or subject to eligibility, rather than simply telling residents that it doesn't exist.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: Please ensure that residents with disabilities receive accurate information and applicable exceptions and reasonable accommodations while reporting applications, denials, and successful purchases.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: Basically, we just want a clear path to have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: home ownership ourselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: That's basically what I came today, but I also wanted to add a little bit extra about the inspection process of Section 8 homes in general.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: The Section 8 inspectors are lacking.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: They let houses pass inspections that really shouldn't.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: You know, I don't know whether it's just incompetence or just they don't care about the job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: My roommate and I moved into a place and it was not up to standards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: There was no light in the place, so we really couldn't see so well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: And they assured us that the place would be put in order by the time we moved in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: But once we were in there, we were just stuck with a landlord who doesn't care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: Up to today, he still doesn't even respond to complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: We have to do 311 in order to get him to come evaluate anything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Morris Lundy
utterances.text: Thank you very much for hearing me today.

chapters.summary: Louise, an HDFC shareholder for 30 years, describes her building's abandonment and conversion to HDFC, which was made possible by the DAMP tax exemption. She asks the council to vote yes on Resolution 9 to renew the tax benefit.
chapters.title: Louise testifies on HDFC history and need for DAMP renewal

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone in attendance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: My name is Louise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: I am a shareholder of the HPD building for 30 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: My family has lived in the building for 75 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: The building was abandoned by the landlord, like so many buildings in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: Barely needs of repairs and bad tenants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: New York City tried to manage these buildings, giving us the opportunity to manage our own buildings, made repairs, taking care of the legal actions, keeping it affordable, keeping a place to live,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: was possible by one of the essential resources given to us at the time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: Was at the time becoming the HDFC, and this was the damp tax exemption.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: And me as a single parent, a single mother at the time, it was certainly a blessing because at that time my husband committed suicide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: Let me tell you, we, HPD,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: HPD shareholders in Brooklyn support the Jackson Taylor Self-Determination Preservation and Affordable Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: S-80 slash A207.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: Please, City Council, vote yes and to renew the tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: For our lives, for our homes, for the affordability, we depend on you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: And also we understand where you have these developers that have done this considerable damage to these housings and things of that nature.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: New York City, big city, lawyers, everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: Why is it that he's allowed to continue?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: do what he do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: That doesn't make sense to me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: It doesn't make sense where you're talking about scamming and taking people's titles away.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: With all the laws and everything that we have in the lawyers, it's impossible for them to say, if somebody is getting a thing, why can't you inform the homeowner?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: Somebody is just taking this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: They find out everything else.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: They take your home from you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: So why can't they find this?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: I don't understand that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: Another thing, too, that we understand, too, with HPD, want to demand the HPDs to sign a regulatory agreement in order, if they don't, then they want to take away the damp tanks from you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Louise
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And actually, so Morris, for you, one of the things maybe we could follow up on is to look into the staffing numbers, because I'm curious to know about that as well in terms of the inspectors.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So that would be good to know.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And Sabrina, just to echo, 421A is very much important to the city council and making sure that that continues.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Sharice, I'm also a graduate of Columbia Social Work School, so yay.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: We need more social workers in government, just FYI.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And Louise, thank you so much for, you know, in terms of the supporting.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: You know, of the buildings and the conditions that it's in, that actually happened to my great aunt and the complex that she was in.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And it took forever for us to even get the landlords to help.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And so I just wanted to say here.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: frustration and these are things that on the council side we really are trying to hopefully these bills will help to improve some of those things so thank you all for coming

chapters.summary: Linda Lee calls the next panel. A proxy reads testimony from Gay Mamula, an HDFC shareholder, who urges passage of Resolution 9 and the state bill S880B/A2707B. She emphasizes that the bill preserves existing income limits and DAMP tax relief without shifting rules.
chapters.title: Panel called: Ud Heinemann, Donald Smith, Diane Orr, Juliana Hess; Gay Mamula's testimony urges Resolution 9

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, next we have you'd.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: E-U-D.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I'm sorry if I'm mispronouncing it.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Ud Heinemann, Donald Smith, Diane Orr, Juliana Hess.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Yeah, I called you before.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I did, I did.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Yeah, sorry if I didn't say it loud enough.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, yes, feel free to go ahead in whichever order.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I'm going to start.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I'm here to present on behalf of someone who couldn't stay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: She had to go back to work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: She only had an hour and had to run back to her reception desk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: So here I go.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Dear Chair Sanchez, Chair Lee, and members of the Committee on Housing and Buildings and the Committee on Finance, my name is Gay Mamula.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I'm a longtime New Yorker, an Upper West resident, and an HDFC shareholder.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I'm writing to urge you to please pass Resolution 9, calling on our state lawmakers to pass

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: S-880B-A-2707B, the HDFC Fairness, Preservation, and Affordability Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: In my HDFC, we enforce income limits on new buyers, and we rely on the damn tax cap and the rest of the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: rules we agreed to when we bought our homes to keep our main...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: affordable and our buildings in good shape.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: By preserving existing income restrictions in exchange for dam tax relief, the S880B-A2707

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: abides by the signed contract between HDFC homeowners and the city without shifting the rules after the fact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Keeping monthly maintenance affordable so working New Yorkers and retirees can stay in their homes is what preserving affordability looks like.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I urge you to keep what's working and reject suggestions to impose new restrictions that would ultimately make our buildings unaffordable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Stand with HDFC shareholders and our communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Please vote yes to Resolution 9.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Go ahead.

chapters.summary: Donald Smith, a retired FDNY firefighter and HDFC shareholder, describes his fixed income and variable rate mortgage. He asks the council to pass Resolution 9 to prevent further financial strain.
chapters.title: Donald Smith testifies on impact of DAMP expiration on fixed income

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: My name is Donald Smith.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: I'm a shareholder at 3810 Broadway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: I'm new to this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: I don't have something to submit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: I'm just going from my heart, sharing with you how this would impact me and my family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: We have lived in 3810.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: For the last, oh, I'd say 10 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: And I personally feel that this dam tax, if they don't approve it, it's going to impact me financially.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: Okay, first thing is, I'm just recently, after serving 15 years with the New York City Fire Department, just retired October 30th.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: Now, anybody knowing retirement, you have to plan your budget very tightly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: Now, after overcoming our 10-year mortgage, we had a 10-year mortgage deal with a lending institution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: It expired last year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: So then now we have a variable rate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: Okay, so that is something you plan for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: So we plan for that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: But now, with this damn tax not being approved, it's going to be even more difficult for me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: You know, I mean, like I said, you base your retirement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: And anybody knows with the city, you get so much in retirement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: So it's a fixed income.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: And my only reason that I did retire after 15 years of service was because of a medical reason.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: I was having a lot of medical challenges in the last year or so.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: But I want to be here to let everyone know that we can do this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: We can pass this regulation, Resolution 9, because it's beneficial to the citizens and the people of New York City who serve for the city, who have served their country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: I served in the military for 11 years, came back to New York, wanted to buy a home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: We could have went to Staten Island, but we said, no, we'll stay in New York because my wife is from the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: She was there when the Bronx was burning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: So she wanted to say, let's stay in New York City so we can make a difference in our family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: So please, pass Resolution 9.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Donald Smith
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Diane Orr, board member of an HDFC in the East Village, describes an aging-in-place cooperative where two-thirds of residents are 80-90 years old. Their real estate tax bill has tripled in five years, pushing them toward default, and she asks for support of Resolution 9.
chapters.title: Diane Orr testifies on aging co-op and rising tax burden

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: My name is Diane Orr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: I am a board member and officer of Florisol 641 East 11th Street HDFC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: We are homesteaders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: And I first want to thank the entire council for some of the most provocative questions that were asked.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: This afternoon of the Department of Finance and of HPD Commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: I am here to ask you to support the resolution known as 009

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: in support of HDFC Fairness, Preservation, and Affordability Act, also referred to as S-88.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: 0B, which renews damp tax exemption without letting Citi and HPD strip away our HDFC self-determination.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: We remain at Florisol 641 a self-managed co-op, and this will protect our affordable homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: We entered in 1990, received our permanent certificate of occupancy,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: but we have become an aging-in-place cooperative, with almost two-thirds of our residents 80 to 90 years of age, and with the remaining, I'm the 80,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: With the remaining one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: One-third with those folks over 65.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: Our real estate tax bill has almost tripled in the last five years,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: and the pass-along to individuals of these retired ages is not only a burden, but an expense that we all may not be able to meet, pushing us to the brink of default.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: And possible foreclosure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: We need your help to deal with the Department of Finance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Orr
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Rachel Ciprian, co-founder of the Black Homeowners Preservation Coalition, describes her 18-year fight to get her deed back after being scammed. She criticizes the lack of accountability for deed theft perpetrators and calls for enforcement of existing laws.
chapters.title: Rachel Ciprian testifies on deed theft and racial injustice

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: Thank you for having this meeting, this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: And like she said, you guys asked some really provocative questions of the Department of Finance and the other woman that was here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: And my name is Rachel Ciprian.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: I am with Black Homeless Preservation Coalition, along with Cherise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: She founded it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: I'm the co-founder.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: And women of Stop Deep Death Movement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: I'm here today and listening to everyone's concern.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: But our concern is, like Cherise said, Brooklyn is no longer black.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: Where we were is fast disappearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It is unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: Deep theft is real.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It is harmful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It is more than just stealing a title to a home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It's taking away generational wealth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It's taking away security, your mental health, stability, everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It is horrible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: This reminds me of Tulsa.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It reminds me of Rosewood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It reminds me of the damage that continues to happen to people who look like me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It is sickening and it needs to stop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: This is not rocket science.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It's not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: We have bills on the book right now that could have helped the Terrain Robinson family, should have helped her, 756A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: We have an attorney general who is not doing her job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: not being held accountable, and neither is Hakeem Jeffries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: And all the people that are supposed to protect us are not protecting us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: So in essence, we're putting into a system, we pay taxes, and we're getting our behinds kicked.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It is unacceptable, and it needs to stop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: I'm in my home 28 years, and I think I've been fighting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: For the last 18 years to have my deed returned to me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: That is unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: When we look at the record and we see what was done to me, I thought I was doing a loan modification and I got scammed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: This is not okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: This is America.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: Not okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: Enforce the laws that are on the books, and when people like Sanford Sony steal homes in Brooklyn and in Queens and is convicted and sentenced to only two to six years, whereas if my husband,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: not that I have one, or my son or my brother or a black man

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: committed the same crime, he'd be in jail forever.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: So we can't have two Americas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: We can't have that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: None of these homes have been returned to some of my comrades in my coalition that should have their home back, should be whole again, should be able to live their lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: They can't.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: Because their deeds have been stolen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: This man was convicted and sentenced to two to six years and only served two months and is out on bail.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: And for all we know,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: He's probably in Israel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: This is unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: That building that collapsed the other day is an exposure of the dark money.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: This building had so many violations, yet they're allowed to do whatever they want at our expense.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: Because this did not happen in Borough Park.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It didn't happen in Park Slope.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It didn't happen in Midwood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It happened in Flatbush, Black Flatbush, what's left of it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: Unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: Eight people died.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: We do not matter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: It's disgusting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: And this needs to be taken care of and taken care of fast.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: People in my community are working only to pay rent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Ciprian
utterances.text: That building that was going to go up, no one in black Brooklyn would have been able to afford it anyway.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you, Rachel, Charisse, for the work you guys are doing in the community because that is much, much needed.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And to your point, Charisse, earlier, the protection piece is what we really need for a lot of the homeowners and the accountability piece, too.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: To your point.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And then for the older adults, NORCs, increasing costs.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: By the way, Donald, you did a great job for your first time.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I just wanted to give kudos to you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: But thank you all for just coming and sharing your personal stories because this is actually what we need to help advance a lot of the things that I know the deputy speaker and I have talked a lot.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: A lot about wanting to reform the property tax system, which is very broken.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And a lot of the housing laws we have in place definitely disproportionately impact black and brown families, the ones in my district as well in Southeast Queens.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So that is something that we are going to continue to look at.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: But I just want to thank you all for coming to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sabrina Lam
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So we have, oh yeah, no, no, no, it's not over, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: We have a few more panels.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: We have a lot more panels.

chapters.summary: Linda Lee calls the next panel. Victoria Morgan, a first-time homebuyer in Brooklyn, describes buying a house with no certificate of occupancy and 23 open HPD violations, which was not disclosed. She asks for a single accountable coordinator for property transaction fraud victims.
chapters.title: Panel called: V. Morgan, Pascale Toussaint, Lorraine Pette, Peter Green; Victoria Morgan testifies on undisclosed violations

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, so we have V.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Morgan, Pascale Toussaint, Lorraine Pette, and Peter Green, both as himself, and also on behalf of Eva Heinemann.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So you're representing two people today.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Sorry, this is just the next panel.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: We have more, don't worry.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Yavie Morgan, Pascale Toussaint, Lorraine Pett, and Peter Green.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, perfect.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And each of you will get two minutes.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I know you're speaking on behalf of yourself and others, but if you could just shorten it a little bit.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Good afternoon chairs and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: My name is Victoria Morgan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: I am an immigrant, a first-time home buyer in Brooklyn, and I am what happens when documented violations are treated as paperwork and immigrants are sold the Brooklyn Bridge.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Last week, eight New Yorkers, including two children, died when 1321 Flatbush Avenue collapsed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: That building had 98 open violations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: The contractor next door had paid a $10,000 fine for working through a stop work order.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: And kept working.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: The Mayor has pledged to hold everyone responsible, fully accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: I am asking you to build that accountability before the next collapse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: My case is the same failure, but one chapter earlier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: In January 2020,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: I bought a Brooklyn house.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: City records show no certificate of occupancy, a Department of Buildings partial vacay order, and 23 open HPD violations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: The house could not lawfully be occupied.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: No one in the property transaction or at the closing table disclosed that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: They sold me a house that I couldn't live in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: The title insurer insured over it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: The lender funded despite its possession of the title report.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: And the attorneys drafted a $35,000 escrow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: funded by my own down payment, nowhere in the HUD-1 closing disclosure, to force the closing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Six years on, every agency has checked its box and no one owns the disastrous outcome.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: I need to finish.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: The attorneys who received $4 million in funding declined my case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Of deep theft prevention attorney referral when unanswered after I provided the required information and followed up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: The Brooklyn District Attorney recently opened an inquiry but never invoked the RPAPL 756A

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: which would require the court to stay even the foreclosure judgment while that investigation continues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Fighting this fraud has become my full-time, unpaid job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: So, in summary, I say pass intro 1091, intro 1096, and intro 1097.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Then I need you to go further.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Intro 1096 already names the Mayor's Office of Deep Death Prevention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Give that or an adjacent office one more duty.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: A single accountable coordinator for property transaction fraud victims.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: so that the next buyer is not told at every door that they would sold the Brooklyn Bridge and fell through the cracks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: I will submit a written protocol for the record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Peter Green, an HDFC shareholder in Washington Heights, rebuts criticisms of Resolution 9, arguing it doesn't raise income limits, price caps would harm financing, and it extends tax relief to more buildings. He asks the council to pass Resolution 9 without changes and reads a statement from Eva Heinemann.
chapters.title: Peter Green defends Resolution 9 as written, rebuts criticisms

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Hi.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: My name is Peter Green.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: I'm here with the HDFC Coalition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: My wife and two kids and I have a HDFC co-op in Washington Heights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Thanks, Councilmember Lee, for being the last survivor here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: It's kind of like everyone else left the island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: We really appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Look, I want to respond to a few concerns and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: falsehoods, misunderstandings, misrepresentations that you've heard today about S-880B.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: I'm here to support passing Resolution 9, urging you to support the passage of Resolution 9 without making any more changes and mucking around with it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Okay, first off, lasting affordability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: The bill doesn't raise anyone's income limits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: It writes the existing limits into law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Is there too much echo here?
