utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: It writes the existing limits into law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: As long as a building receives the tax benefits, every buyer must meet the income formula already in state law or the AMI limit in the building's own documents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: The income limits works.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: HDFC is sold on average for 61%

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: of comparable Manhattan co-ops from 2020 to 2024.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: We do have data on this, despite what other people say.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: The bill doesn't put new resale caps on homes we already own.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Price caps would make HDFCs harder to finance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: The math just doesn't math.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Once you put price caps on, you become limited equity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: You can't get private financing from a bank.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: You have to pay higher terms because you're riskier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: People will be underwater.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Buildings will be underwater.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Mortgages from both individuals and buildings will be unable to be paid, and the buildings will go into bankruptcy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: The first victims are going to be elderly residents on fixed income.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Second, about equitable benefits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: People are saying, oh, more tax relief for the wealthier buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: This bill extends tax relief to more buildings, to all HDFCs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: There's a whole bunch right now that don't get any tax relief, and HPD and all their contractors you've heard from haven't cared for 40 years when this problem's been staring them in the face.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Can I just...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: A little bit more, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Finally, accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: There is zero accountability right now from HPD, from HDFCs to HPD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: We put it in the bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: The last thing I want to say is there are two groups of HDFCs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: As the commissioner said, there are 1,150 HDFCs that are doing just fine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Don't mess the rules around on them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Let them continue to thrive and provide relatively affordable housing for New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: There's 250 in trouble.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: We don't prevent them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: from having regulatory agreements, this bill won't prevent anyone who gets into trouble from working closely with HPD and setting up new restrictions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: And when you get these TPT buildings, we're here to give you our lived experience to make that a better version than the thing that was hastily cobbled together in the 1970s by the Koch administration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: And we can talk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Offline about this and we'll follow more about it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: But we're asking you, please just support Sean's bill, resolution 880B as it is, and then move on to the next thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Don't sacrifice, you know, don't let the perfect be the enemy of the good.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Okay, that's it for me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Ava Heinemann, who lives in an HDFC down in the Lower East Side, had to go to a doctor's appointment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: She looks to be quite...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: A senior, so she asked me if I could read a little bit of her statement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: I'll just read the key part of it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: She's a proud senior New Yorker, East Village resident, asking you to pass a Resolution 9 as is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: She said, we were part of a tenants association during the tenement interim

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: interim lease years, helping transform an abandoned, neglected building into a safe, stable, resident-run home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: All the way back in 1980 when we were Alphabet City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: I remember being in high school down there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: It was crazy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: No one would go near this neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: It was a crime and drug-ridden, but thanks to our sweat equity, we turned this into a neighborhood that everyone wants to live in now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Why should we be punished for making this place livable for all the rich kids, but not for us who are still scraping by?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: This is the big thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: 1,150 of these buildings have been...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: been successful, why punish the people who are doing it?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Why not come to us and say, hey, you know, what can you teach us for the next generation?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: And the main thing is affordability, as Eva says, is for the people who live in these buildings, not some constituent who wants a home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: She says, my son grew up in our HDFC building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: It's the only home he has ever known.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: And you want to take it away from him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: I can't leave him much, but I can make sure he always has a place to live.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: And since I got 50 seconds, I was talking to one of my neighbors on the subway today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: She's got a learning disabled son and she and her wife and have two kids.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: And she said, I really hope when I'm gone, sorry, she said, I really hope I can leave from this apartment because otherwise I don't know what I'll do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Anyway, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Let's talk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Let's actually have dialogue with the shareholders, not with the contractors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Go ahead.

chapters.summary: Lorraine Petty, a homeowner, describes being misled by an HPD-approved nonprofit that turned a grant into a subprime loan with 18% interest and a 10-year lien. She asks how nonprofits are vetted and calls for accountability.
chapters.title: Lorraine Petty testifies on fraudulent nonprofit loan and UCC lien

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Hello, my name is Lorraine Petty, and I'm here in support of 2026-2635 Homeowner Protection.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Why must we wait?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: For

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: That's okay, sweetie.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: You good?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Yeah, she's good.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Why must homeowners wait for protection after foreclosure proceeding?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Is there a transparent complaint process and legal counsel provided by HPD to prevent nonprofit and for-profit noncompliance to the law?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: They are giving nonprofits and for-profits a great deal of involvement and control over contractors, funds, repair outcome, coupled with liens placed on individuals'homes that burdens a homeowner.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: A fiduciary duty should be mandatory and outlined.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: I have been involved in litigation as a pro se arising from the misconduct of an HPD-approved nonprofit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: The organization advertised a grant for emergency home repairs and then fraudulently restructured that grant into an unconscionable subprime loan carrying 18% interest at the closing table.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: The nonprofit's malicious involvement resulted in damage to my property while imposing a 10-year lien permitting the nonprofit and its assignees an indefinite security interest in my home while the property continues to deteriorate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Just remember the elements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Distressed property, emergency repairs, fraudulent loan agreement,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: failure to complete repairs, and a 10-year lien, which prevents a homeowner

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: from correcting the faulty repairs due to a third lien position for an additional loan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: This scheme is diabolically genius in a warning for the abuse and mismanagement of HPD's approved nonprofits and for-profits in a bowl of plate that could be used to swindle homes from hard...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Working New Yorkers that are being excluded from the process and denied adequate protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: The legal precedents that are presented to receive justice for the nonprofit's many violations were neither investigated nor given due consideration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Instead, they were dismissed and disregarded by HPD and council members, attorney general, and the court.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Many attorneys are unwilling to take on prolonged disputes involving HPD and nonprofit entities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: I have attached documents supporting my testimony and federal rules.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: I just want to say one thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: How are these nonprofits and for-profits vetted?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: How are they investigated?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: How are they audited?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: This, I believe, a lot of nonprofits and for-profits are the segue to D-DEP.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Because according to the documents that I have,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: They have indefinite interest in my home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: I have brought this to the attorney general.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: I've been in court as a pro se by myself, just like someone else said.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: This is a full-time job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: And thank God, thank God I'm retired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Early retirement from disability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Because the whole thing is, I walked in there for a grant, and I came out the revolving doors with a loan with an 18% interest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: I have an 850 credit score.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: There's no way I would have went to the corner bodega for a loan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: That's what I call it, a corner bodega.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: You gave me a loan, a subprime loan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: If you read these documents, I put them in front of the court.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: And the territory is exactly right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: But what I'm telling you, if you read these documents, you will see.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Let me just read one thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Because it's just, I will give you this documentation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: But let me just tell you what the UCC lien.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: A lot of people don't know what the implications are for UCC lien.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: But let me tell you what this nonprofit wrote.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: It was supposed to be for emergency VPS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: This is their commitment letter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: I'm not going to mention their name because I'm in court.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: But they said to file a UCC financing statement and any amendments and continuation statements in connection with this transcript.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: That means that they can continue this and I waived all rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: But what you have to understand is I was approved for two grants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: They withdrew the grants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Did not complete.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Did not complete the construction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Faulty construction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Now I'm left.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: And I know compared to everyone's problems, this is not big.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: But what I'm saying is I'm not waiting until I'm 75 to be sitting up in court.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: I'm going to stop them beforehand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: And that's why I started this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Situation way beforehand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: I'm not going to wait.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: This ends in 2028.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: But just like I said, they can extend this UCC lien and therein lies the problem.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So sorry, not to interrupt because I know we have to move on to other panels, but if you could actually submit that documentation, because I, I, I,

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: As someone who ran nonprofit organizations for 20 years, we have so many audits and regulatory things that we have to go through on our end.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So I'm curious to see where that fell off.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: You know what I mean?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Because there are a ton of audits that we have to go through with multiple agencies.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So I'd be curious to look at that a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And then, Victoria, also your case, too.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I know you said you were going to submit more documentation, but I'd be interested to see that also in follow-up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Well, all I want to add.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: I've went through so many channels.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Legal Aid Society, Attorney General, Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: I mean, I sent you all pamphlets with this information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Not one feedback.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: This is so wrong.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: Because just like I said, this is the segue to deep theft and swindling people's homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: That's what this is.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: And I work too damn hard by myself for that home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: And he's not getting it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: I'm not moving.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: But his, my question, my bottom line is with you, because you can't handle the court case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: He needs to be removed with the UCC3 amendment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: He needs to get off because he didn't fulfill his job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: He didn't complete the contract.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: He withdrew funds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: This is wrong.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: And he's stealing business under a different name.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Miss Lee, I will submit, but one thing I want to add is buying a house shouldn't lead to a civil rights issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: My case is now a civil rights issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Immigrants shouldn't be put through this.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Agreed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lorraine Petty
utterances.text: No one should be put through this.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Agreed.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: No one, yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Agreed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Nobody should be put through this.

chapters.summary: Linda Lee calls the next panel. Patricia Orguilagos, a disabled resident of Rosedale, describes ongoing identity theft, deed theft, benefit fraud, and housing irregularities affecting her and her children. She asks for an independent review and coordination among city, state, and federal agencies.
chapters.title: Panel called: Jose Kulin, Kevin Rabinovich, Tanya Taylor, Albert Zambetti; Patricia Orguilagos testifies on identity theft

utterances.text: Okay, next we have Jose Kulin, Kevin Rabinovich, Tanya Taylor, and Albert Zambetti.

utterances.text: Thank you to give me the opportunity to tell my case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: I am from Rosedale.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos

utterances.text: respectfully request that the appropriate investigator determine whether there were unauthorized change, claims, payment, enrollment, representative, or other misuse of my identity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: I know HRA funds were improperly obtained in my name for appropriate two years without my authorization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: I also request a review of my Section 8 housing voucher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: Payment record, because I believe and I know the voucher or related housing payment have been associated with a different property address from the unit where I reside.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: I have repeatedly reported incident of harassment and public lewdness to the city of, to New York City Police Department.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: I respectfully request that those reports be reviewed together with my complaint concerning identity theft, cyber relation activity, benefit and housing record, so that the overall pattern

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: I have reported can be properly evaluated.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: This individual lives downstairs from me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: And he is illegally in this country on a fraud American passport.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: What is he doing downstairs from me is stealing people's identity and affecting all people on top of it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: It needs to stop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: They need to arrest this guy.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: My address is 25921 Francis Lewis Boulevard, and he live on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Orguilagos
utterances.text: You guys need to do something about it, or I will.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you, Patricia.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Victoria Morgan
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: An unnamed speaker supports Resolution 9, discussing the importance of trust and warning against over-regulation. He argues for giving every HDFC the resources they need rather than redistributing limited funds.
chapters.title: Speaker testifies on trust and over-regulation in HDFC legislation

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for the chance to speak this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I firmly stand behind Resolution 009 as it coheres with Senate bill in the New York State Senate,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: 880B and the House Resolution 2707B.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And the idea behind this is that it's a question of trust, I think, in a number of ways, because with the housing bubble,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: the real estate companies and so forth, with coveted assets becoming greater and greater in either real or nominal value

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: across the city, there are more and more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I guess you would say legalese, you know, I don't want to call them scams, but workarounds to carve out the procurement of these properties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And when we talk about changes to the stipulations that we signed up for, when we signed our proprietary leases, when we signed our documents to become shareholders

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I think it's opening a big can of worms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Somebody mentioned earlier the term redistribution in terms of the tax abatements, the damp tax abatements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I don't know if it's simply a question of semantics, but I would not use the term redistribution because that implies limited resources.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I would say you give everybody, every single HDFC, the amount of funding, the amount of abatement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The amount of resources that they need to live a productively comfortable, healthy, developing life, and to manage these buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And that is, I think, the responsibility of legislation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Yeah, I think that's what I would say where the idea of over-regulation, especially when trust is at an all-time low,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: becomes anything but transparent and opens itself up to suspicion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: So once again, I cast my vote strongly for Resolution 009.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: A speaker notes that the city council's online testimony submission system was down, preventing many from submitting. He reads a statement in support of Resolution 9, emphasizing the security and stability HDFCs provide for seniors on fixed incomes.
chapters.title: Speaker notes system outage, supports Resolution 9

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Hi, I'm just going to keep this short because everybody wants to go home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: But I just wanted to let you know that I wanted to do this in writing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And since last night up until like 11 o'clock this morning, I could not submit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Your system is down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: So there's a lot of people you're not hearing from.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And I did it on your form for the city council thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: So I just want to let you know that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I'm going to just read the first paragraph of what I was going to send you, and then I'll make a comment on it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: So I'm writing in support of, and strong support of, City Council Resolution 9 for HDFCs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I currently divide it in an efficient, self-governing, and well-managed co-op in Hell's Kitchen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: As a senior citizen with limited income, my home provides me with a measure of security and stability that I cannot afford to lose.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: At 70, I work a nearby part-time job to supplement my Social Security.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And I'm an active member of my community, all of which I think would be in jeopardy if we screw around with the damn tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And my further comment is that just out of practicality, I think a lot of people here are born and bred New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I was born in East New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I've driven a cab in New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I kind of worked my way into my HDF scene.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Just in terms of practicality, I remember all these villages.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The block I live on now in Hell's Kitchen, I would not walk on the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: When I went there as a kid, I'd walk in the street because people would...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Jump off the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I think I was mugged there once.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I saw it there once.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: But just the HPD people, and they're doing some of the stuff they do is really good, but wanting to change the damn pack, just in terms of...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I'm not versed in any of this, but turns in practicality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: There's no bonfire on 7th Street anymore.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: We can walk down that street at night.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Why would you want to change?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: anything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: So these areas that I'm going into now, Hell's Kitchen that I'm familiar with and the East Village, the change that has

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: come over them in terms of security and is letting me kind of live there in peace, I think largely has to do with HDFCs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thanks for letting us know the system wasn't working.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thankfully, we have up to 72 hours until after today's hearing to submit, so that still will be available, and we'll definitely look into that.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So thanks.

chapters.summary: Linda Lee calls the next panel. Denise Caniff, an HDFC shareholder in Washington Heights, explains her building's reliance on flip tax income for capital repairs. She supports S880B/A2707B, which enforces AMI limits and ties them to DAMP benefits, and urges passage of Resolution 9.
chapters.title: Panel called: M. Lutel, Denise Keniff, Michael Bucci, and others; Denise Caniff testifies on flip tax and DAMP

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, and next we have M.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Lutel.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Denise Keniff and Michael Bucci.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, so M.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Lutel, Denise Caniff, and Michael Bucci.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And we can add Jamelio de Blas.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, actually let's go ahead and add one more since it seems like folks are missing.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Tina DeFelsi Antonio.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, Duncan Christopher?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And then also, if Cheryl Douglas is here,

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Oh, you have Tina.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Tina?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Okay, you can start.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: Thank you, Council Member.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: My name is Denise Caniff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: I live in an HDAC co-op in Washington Heights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: I'm a shareholder, and I'm testifying in support of Resolution 9 and State Bills S-880B and A-2707B.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: I'm going to get in the weeds just a little bit about my building that will put a lot of what you heard today in perspective.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: My HDFC board has a legal duty to keep our building solvent and safe, but any new government-imposed resale caps would tie their hands.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: Price caps would nearly eliminate my HDFC's flip income.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: tax, which we rely on to fund major capital repairs for our 118-year-old building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: The reserve funds from our flip tax income are currently paying for our

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: elevator and that's being installed right now and a new roof scheduled to be replaced in five years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: Without the flip tax income, my board would be forced to hit us with massive maintenance hikes or assessments we simply can't afford.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: Likewise, without damp tax, our monthly maintenance would skyrocket, pricing out working class New Yorkers and seniors on fixed incomes, the majority of our building, who many have saved our building from collapse in the 80s and 90s when they were in the TIL program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: The state bills S-880B and A-270B protect long-term affordability by doing two things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: The state bill allows, enforces the AMI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: It actually adds affordability in it, not the opposite of what you heard today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: So, for example, my existing building has 120% AMI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: It's written in it to our governing documents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: It would be tied to forever the damp tax benefit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: Along with that, there's the annual HPD compliance audit, which our building also is already required to do, and we comply every year with HPD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: I first learned about HPD's new resale caps back in 2016.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: I urge you to keep what's working and reject suggestions to impose new restrictions that would completely change our HDSIC co-op governing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: After a decade of uncertainty, we have waited long enough, and the damp property tax is expiring in 2029, so clarity is urgent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: The extension of the damp tax property provides equitable benefits, unlike what you heard today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: Those familiar with the bill agree it extends the relief to more buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: Buildings with higher assessments, such as mine, face higher taxes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: But our income limits, because we're income limited, HDFC, because we're from the TILA program, are the same.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: We have the same rules.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: My building, which is larger, we have a higher tax assessment because we provide more affordable apartments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: So don't change the structure of the damp tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: It works.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: It's being expanded so it can work for more HDFC buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: Please pass Reso 9 this year and preserve one of the most successful affordable housing programs in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Denise Caniff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Green
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Jana Liu de Blas, an HDFC shareholder and researcher, shares her experience with landlord neglect and the safety of her HDFC. She opposes price caps, arguing they would destroy the mixed-income model, and says UHAB funding should go to maintenance instead of education.
chapters.title: Jana Liu de Blas testifies on HDFC model and opposition to price caps

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: My name is Jana Liu de Blas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: I'm a shareholder.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: I live in 144 in Amsterdam and also a researcher and a writer of the blog Civid Gaps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: I would like you to go there and to see the text I wrote on the appropriation of housing by HPD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: I have three reasons for asking you to pass Resolution 9.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: First reason, I'm talking about my own experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: When I first moved to New York, I actually moved to Harlem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: I noticed that it was a rent stabilized.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: I noticed that the lock in my building were not working.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: I put several complaints and then I realized by myself why they were not working.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: It was profitable for my landlord to bring criminals in so we move out and he can increase the rent 20%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: I was raping my building and after being raping my building I have one thing in mind.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: I want a building with no landlord.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: I moved to another building in the same area but it was an

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: HDSC and it was safer, almost the same neighborhood and it was safer because people living on it were taking care of everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: They wanted to make the neighborhood better.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: We put trees in the streets, we keep things working.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: We need no landlords.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: We don't want HPD to be our landlord.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: We don't want UHF to be our landlord.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: The twin building next to mine now is also owned by HPD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: It's a disaster.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: Let me just tell one second argument that is really important.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: We need to have cash prices off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: And this is why.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: In my building, it's 20 units, 12 people is on section 8 when the roof needs to be replaced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: They didn't have to pay the assessment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: How was working?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: It didn't work because the rest of us paid for the assessment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: The good thing about HDSC model is that the income is mixed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: We don't want cut cells because that will totally destroy the model.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: We need different incomes level because otherwise when something breaks,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: We cannot fix.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: And let me just say one more thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: Seven millions are going to UHAP right now for education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: Our building is doing great.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: We don't need education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: This money will go to maintenance because the prices are skyrocketing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: We don't want the non-for-profit to get rich out of us.

chapters.summary: Duncan Christopher, a pioneer of his HDFC building, describes moving to New York with $75 and transforming apartments. He speaks for the next generation of underfunded New Yorkers and asks to preserve the HDFC model.
chapters.title: Duncan Christopher testifies on transforming buildings and HDFC legacy

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: Hello, my name is Duncan Christopher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: I'm the last living pioneer of a building that was started by Gloria Milliken, who founded HCC, Housing Conservation Coordinators.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: I moved to New York at 19 with $75, and Jimmy Ganitas was the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: Greek guy that owned all these slum landlord buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: So when I tell people, if you've seen Midnight Cowboy, I bought into Ratso Rizzo's apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: Between my two brothers and I, we transformed five apartments on West 48th between 9th and 10th.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: So when I had the opportunity to move down the street and become my own landlord, I'm in a little eight-unit building, and I've been there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: We're...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: started HCC between Clinton and Chelsea neighborhoods.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: So we really transformed the block.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: Across the street was an empty lot where everybody threw their garbage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: We cleaned out the lot and made it the Clinton Community Garden, which is now an award-winning park.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: So I'm here to honor

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: people that have paid the dues, paid the price to become their own landlords.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: And I speak for letting the next generation of people that were really underfunded like me when I came to New York.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you all for sharing your personal stories.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And Gemma, thank you for sharing your story.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And I'm so sorry that that happened to you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: But yes, I appreciate you coming here today and sharing.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: And I'm sorry I didn't have anything written down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: Oh, no, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: I just speak my heart.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And if you change your mind and you still want to submit written testimony, you have 72 hours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duncan Christopher
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Is Vernon Ballard here?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, is anyone here that didn't sign up to testify that would like to testify?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: If you could say your name.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jana Liu de Blas
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Cheryl Douglas, a member of the HDFC Coalition leadership committee, describes how HDFCs allowed her to buy into her community. She opposes new restrictions and price caps, and asks the council to pass Resolution 9 as written.
chapters.title: Cheryl Douglas urges support for Resolution 9 as written

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: Okay, good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: My name is Cheryl Douglas, and I am a part of the leadership committee of the HDFC Coalition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: And I'm here today to ask that you...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: That you keep what works and give your support to Councilman

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: Abreu's Resolution 9, urging the state legislature to pass the HDFC Fairness, Preservation, and Affordability Act as written and with nothing more added to it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: The HDFC program is near and dear to my heart because it allowed me to remain and buy into the community in which I was born and raised and for me to give back to that community as a teacher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: In the 80s and 90s, many landlords walked away from the buildings, leaving them in various stages of disrepair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: The HDFC shareholders repaired those buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: They invested in the buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: They put blood, sweat, and tears into those buildings for an investment so that they could pass that on to their heirs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: Now, what seems to be at stake is we might lose all of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: Now that the dam tax break that helped keep our co-op.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: affordable expires in 2029.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: HBD is using that as a weapon to force buildings to accept new, much stricter restrictions or lose the benefit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: They want resale price caps, asset caps on owners and new buyers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: They want the heirs who must

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: to meet income and assets-based restrictions to inherit the home in which they grew up and to give HPD the power to replace boards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: This will dismantle and destabilize a very important housing stock.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: Imposing stricter restrictions, price caps, and outside control of privately owned co-ops will fail.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: Past Resolution 9 supporting S-880A-2707, the HDFC Fairness Reservation and Affordability Act, it gives every HDFC a fair tax rate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: It keeps current buyer income limits and adds real reporting and audits with no price caps and, in our view, no fiscal impact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cheryl Douglas
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, so last call.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Is anyone here that did not sign up to testify and would like to?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Yes, it is recorded.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And just wanted to say quickly for those still left in the room, we're moving on to our Zoom online testimony, but I just wanted to say that, and I know Chair Sanchez is still listening online,

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: but just wanted to say that I appreciate all of you coming in and waiting so long to testify and giving us your feedback and sharing your personal stories because it's all very helpful when we're thinking of examples of what is falling through the cracks.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And I know many of you shared very heart-wrenching stories that I know are very personal to you, and I can totally understand and appreciate the mental health and the stress it puts on you and your families.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And so I just wanted to say that, and I know that it's not exactly an answer or consolation, but we are dedicated on the council to really working with you all and partnering.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So this testimony and the feedback you've given is very helpful, so I just wanted to say thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, so we are going to go, and we will try to follow up on some of those that you've given to us.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Jacob Schneider, Senior Program Manager at the East New York Community Land Trust, opposes the administration's plan for a 2027 lien sale. He cites comptroller data showing higher collection rates in years without a sale, and asks the council to hold oversight hearings.
chapters.title: Jacob Schneider opposes 2027 lien sale, cites collection rate data

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Lee, and thank you, Chair Sanchez, for listening in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: My name is Jacob Schneider, and I am the Senior Program Manager for Research and Policy at the East New York Community Land Trust.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: The East New York CLT works to prevent displacement and real estate speculation in the neighborhoods of East New York and Brownsville.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: We are a founding member of the Abolish the New York City Tax Lien Sale Coalition and have been fighting for more than six years to end the predatory lien sale and replace it with a just and equitable system of debt collection.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: The East New York CLT and the Abolish Coalition strongly oppose the administration's plan to hold a lien sale in 2027.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: We have seen and heard from homeowners and tenants how the lien sale makes them targets for predatory speculators, causes unnecessary stress, and allows negligent landlords to continue exploiting vulnerable tenants who are often not covered by tenant protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: We only need to look at the events of last week on Flatbush Avenue, where the landlord has systematically used the lien sale as part of his business model with deadly consequences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: We are asking the City Council to do whatever they can to hold Mayor Mamdani to his campaign promise to end the lien sale on day one and not follow the path of his predecessor who made a similar campaign promise, only to renege on it once in office.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: There is no justification for holding a lien sale in 2027.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: The administration, like those of the past, has made the spurious argument that the lien sale is necessary to enforce tax collection, but the evidence says otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: According to the most recent financial report of the New York City Comptroller, the collection rate was higher in 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2026, all years without a sale, than in 2025 when there was a lien sale.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: The harm of the lien sale on communities of color far outweighs any actual or perceived benefit of holding a lien sale.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: If the administration forages ahead with a lien sale in 2027, we ask that the council conduct regular and ongoing oversight hearings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: The current system is opaque and puts homeowners and tenants in harm's way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: We need to bring transparency to any sale that will occur, and the council can play an important role in doing so.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Jacob.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And totally agree that we want to make sure that these are not punitive and that we can help a lot of the homeowners.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Basha Nikanoro, a first-generation New Yorker and HDFC shareholder, describes how HDFCs allowed her family to buy a home and age in place. She asks the council to pass Resolution 9 in support of the Albany bill.
chapters.title: Basha Nikanoro testifies on HDFC as path to homeownership

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Hi.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Basha Nikanoro, and I am in support of City Council Resolution 9 for HDFCs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: I am a first-generation New Yorker.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: My husband is an immigrant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: We purchased our HDFC apartment on West 137th Street in Hamilton Heights when our kids were young.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: We didn't have generational wealth or trust funds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: We didn't dream of buying a home in New York City until discovering the world of HDFCs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Our building is within easy distance of the grandparents, and we could count on their support as we undertook the daunting task of raising kids in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Now, nearly 20 years later, the tables are turned and we are able to help the grandparents age in place because we are nearby.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: HDFCs ensure age and economic diversity among young family and senior homeowners, contributing to a vibrant urban tapestry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: We've worked hard to achieve 100% compliance with New York City's laws and abide with the HDFC rules and the spirit of HDFCs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: We have put in the hard work of stabilizing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: our HDFC and merit full governance over our co-op.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Our buildings, HDFC residents, represent a microcosm of New York City's working professionals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: We are public school teachers, home health aides, college professors, music teachers, speech therapists, contractors, musicians, actors, clerical workers, food industry workers, filmmakers, and civil servants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: We create the appeal that attracts millions of New Yorkers, tourists, and their dollars to the Big Apple each day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Thus, HDFC's...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: ...Tale of two...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Tale of two cities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Just in conclusion, HDFCs are a force multiplier ensuring mixed income and mixed age neighborhoods, supercharging a vibrant urban human tapestry that ensures that New York City remains a destination for millions of people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Please pass City Council Resolution 9 in support of the Albany Bill S-880BA2707B.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Thank you for this very much, Chair Lee and Councilmember Sanchez, and to all of the committee for hosting this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: It is so important.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: And just to show you how deeply this is felt for our family and my parents, as well as now my kids, I've even written my graduate thesis on the topic of how unique this building stock is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Basha Nikanoro
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

summary: The Committee on Finance, jointly with Housing and Buildings, held an oversight hearing on advancing homeownership opportunity and protection, considering a package of bills and resolutions.
Administration officials from HPD, DOF, and DOB testified on programs, concerns with Intro 1084, lien sale reforms, and property tax reform efforts.

Council members questioned agencies on homeownership production, foreclosure prevention, deed theft, and tax exemptions; public testimony highlighted personal stories of deed theft, HDFC challenges, and calls for stronger protections.

topic: Oversight - Advancing Homeownership Opportunity and Protection
